io: Partial multi-omic cell profile -> cell embeddings and missing-modality generation
status: Paper only; project repository says artifacts are in preparation and licence remains unresolved
use_cases: Multi-omic cell representation, missing-modality prediction and generative integration
audit_note: Identity, scope, primary/official sources and current catalog claims were checked in the changed-record audit; no unresolved material error was recorded.

name: CellOS
description: Large multi-view single-cell joint-embedding predictive model for cell-state representation and perturbation prediction.
io: Single-cell transcriptome -> cell-state embeddings and perturbation predictions
status: Paper only; no public code or weights found
use_cases: Cell-state representation, transfer and perturbation prediction
audit_note: Identity, scope, primary/official sources and current catalog claims were checked in the changed-record audit; no unresolved material error was recorded.

name: OmniCell
description: Tissue-contextual model pretrained across dissociated and spatial expression profiles for unified cellular and molecular representations.
io: Single-cell or spatial expression + tissue context -> unified cell and molecular representations
status: Public source + checkpoint; source MIT and checkpoint labelled Apache-2.0
use_cases: Single-cell and spatial representation, tissue-context transfer and downstream prediction
audit_note: Identity, scope, primary/official sources and current catalog claims were checked in the changed-record audit; no unresolved material error was recorded.

name: BioReason-Pro
description: Protein-function reasoning model combining protein sequence understanding with language-model reasoning and tool/evidence workflows; distinct from the DNA-focused BioReason model.
io: Protein sequence + scientific question/evidence -> multi-step protein-function reasoning
status: MIT code; public Apache-2.0 SFT and RL weights and GO-GPT component; public Apache-2.0 datasets; web interface
use_cases: Protein-function reasoning, annotation, evidence synthesis and mechanistic explanation
audit_note: Identity, scope, primary/official sources and current catalog claims were checked in the changed-record audit; no unresolved material error was recorded. 2026-10-10: code licence confirmed as MIT (LICENSE committed 2026-08-19; GitHub licence API); SFT, RL and GO-GPT weights and the seven datasets in the Hugging Face collection are public and tagged apache-2.0; paper link moved from the redirecting early/ URL to bioRxiv v2 (posted 2026-07-19). Limits: weights were not downloaded or run; the repository README still calls the required ESM3-sm-open-v1 encoder gated, while its Hugging Face card (now biohub/esm3-sm-open-v1) is ungated and states an MIT licence; separate BioReason-Pro v2 uploads on a personal account (adibvafa/bioreason-pro-v2-*, manually gated, cc-by-nc-4.0) are not confirmed as official and are not covered by this record.

name: GENEB
description: Diagnostic benchmark that linear-probes frozen representations from 40 genomic foundation models across 100 DNA classification tasks in 13 functional categories, under full-data, 10-shot, and 1-shot regimes.
status: Open harness + task data (Apache-2.0); public ungated leaderboard
io: Frozen genomic-model embeddings + DNA classification tasks -> per-task, per-category and overall MCC, accuracy and macro-F1 scores
use_cases: Genomic model selection, head-to-head comparison of DNA language models, few-shot representation evaluation
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_1.json. Apache-2.0 covers harness and task data; no gating.

name: PG-LLM
description: ProteinGym-derived benchmark of 217 protein-variant ranking tasks in which a model ranks mutant sequences from the wild-type sequence and an assay description alone, without MSAs or structures, plus a contamination-control panel of 59 assays released after January 2026.
status: Open harness + frozen evaluation bundle (MIT); data released for evaluation use only and the contamination panel is available from the authors on request
io: Wild-type sequence + assay description + shuffled mutant set -> ranked mutants scored by nested-macro Spearman
use_cases: Variant-effect ranking benchmarks for general-purpose and protein language models, contamination-controlled evaluation, leaderboard submission
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_1.json. MIT code; the released data bundle carries an evaluation-only use policy and the 59-assay contamination panel is request-only.

name: Nesso-1
description: Coarse-grained cofolding model from Valence Labs / Recursion that jointly predicts protein-ligand structure and binding affinity in about one second per prediction on a single GPU.
status: Open code + weights (Apache-2.0), ungated
io: Protein sequence + ligand (SMILES, CCD code or SDF) in an input YAML -> binding-affinity scalar, binder/non-binder score and cofolded complex
use_cases: High-throughput virtual screening, binding-affinity prediction, hit triage, selectivity assessment, embedding extraction
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_1.json. Apache-2.0 on both code and weights, no gating.

name: Promera
description: Unified all-atom generative model from the Berger lab (MIT) that combines biomolecular co-folding with binder filtering and controllable minibinder and nanobody design under optional epitope, paratope and template constraints.
status: Open code + weights (MIT), ungated
io: JSON specification of protein, nucleic-acid and ligand chains with optional constraints -> all-atom complex structures, confidence/filtering scores and designed binder sequences
use_cases: All-atom co-folding, de novo binder and nanobody design, binder filtering, epitope-targeted design
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_2.json. MIT on code and weights, no gating.

name: DeCAF (DeCAF-Boltz)
description: Flow-map distillation framework from Genesis Molecular AI that turns all-atom co-folding diffusion models into few-step generators; the released DeCAF-Boltz checkpoint distils Boltz-1 into a few-step sampler, while the DeCAF-Pearl variant is described but not released.
status: Open code + DeCAF-Boltz weights (MIT), ungated; DeCAF-Pearl weights not released
io: Boltz-format complex specification of protein sequences and ligands -> all-atom complex structures generated in a few sampling steps, with confidence scores
use_cases: Fast all-atom co-folding, protein-ligand pose prediction, large-scale structure-based virtual screening
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_2.json. MIT on code and released weights; the teacher model Boltz-1 is itself MIT.

name: FeNNix-Bio1
description: Machine-learning interatomic potential in two sizes (S and M) for atomistic simulation of organic and biological systems, from the Piquemal group, trained on an extension of the SPICE2 quantum-chemistry dataset.
status: Public ungated weights under the Academic Software License: academic non-commercial use only
io: Atomic coordinates and element types -> potential energy and forces for molecular dynamics, optimization and free-energy calculations
use_cases: Molecular dynamics of organic and biological systems, geometry optimization, hydration and binding free-energy calculation, scoring in drug design
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_2.json. The Academic Software Licence explicitly forbids commercial use, so noncommercial is true.

name: CheMatE
description: ModernBERT-based chemistry encoder that places SMILES strings and chemistry natural language in one shared embedding space through continued masked-language pretraining followed by Matryoshka contrastive fine-tuning.
status: Open code + weights (MIT), ungated; evaluation datasets available on request
io: SMILES string or chemistry text -> dense embedding vector
use_cases: Molecular property prediction, chemistry text embedding and retrieval, clustering, frozen-encoder features
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_5.json. MIT on code and both checkpoints, no gating.

name: NovoMolGen
description: Family of Llama-architecture molecular language models (32M, 157M and 300M parameters) pretrained on 1.5 billion ZINC-22 molecules and released with both atom-wise and BPE SMILES tokenizers.
status: Public MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face, ungated; the source repository carries no licence file
io: Start token or partial SMILES -> generated molecule SMILES and hidden-state embeddings
use_cases: De novo molecule generation, goal-directed molecular optimization, reinforcement-learning molecular design
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_6.json. Weights are MIT; no LICENSE file exists in the code repository.

name: ReaSyn (NV-ReaSyn)
description: NVIDIA encoder-decoder model that generates a molecule's synthetic pathway as a sequence over known reactions and building blocks, returning pathways for the closest synthesizable analog when the target itself is not synthesizable; v2 adds an Edit Flow refinement model.
status: Open code (Apache-2.0) + public weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, ungated and commercially usable
io: Molecule SMILES -> synthetic pathway over building blocks for the target or its closest synthesizable analog
use_cases: Synthesis planning, synthesizable analog generation, synthesizability-constrained property optimization
audit_note: Added 2026-08-13 (evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_6.json). 2026-10-10 refresh: the GitHub repository moved from NVIDIA-Digital-Bio to NVIDIA-BioNeMo; the old URL returns a 301 redirect and both Hugging Face cards still link it, so the code link now points to the new location. All row claims re-checked on 2026-10-10: arXiv 2509.16084 (v2 dated 10 Jan 2026), Apache-2.0 repository LICENSE, both v2 Hugging Face checkpoints ungated under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which states models are commercially usable, and v2 release dated 1/8/2026 on the cards. Bundled data (ODbL, CC BY 4.0) and third-party code licences carry no non-commercial terms. The Enamine US Stock building blocks used in the paper are available from Enamine on request.

name: MiniMol
description: Parameter-efficient molecular graph model (about 10M parameters) pretrained on roughly 3,300 quantum and biological graph- and node-level tasks, used as a frozen featurizer producing 512-dimensional fingerprints.
status: Open code + weights (MIT); weights ship in the GitHub repository and the pip package
io: SMILES strings -> 512-dimensional molecular fingerprint embeddings
use_cases: ADMET and molecular property prediction, low-data transfer learning, molecular featurization
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_6.json. One MIT grant covers code and the bundled weights.

name: CheMeleon
description: Molecular foundation model pretrained to predict classical Mordred descriptors rather than experimental or simulated labels, giving a transferable representation usable as a frozen fingerprint or fine-tuned through chemprop.
status: Open code + weights (MIT); weights on Zenodo and auto-downloaded by chemprop
io: SMILES string or RDKit molecule -> molecular embedding, or fine-tuned property prediction
use_cases: Molecular property prediction, ADMET modelling, small-data transfer learning, fingerprint generation
audit_note: Full re-check 2026-10-10. Added the JCIM journal version (DOI 10.1021/acs.jcim.6c01546, online 2026-08-07, same seven authors as arXiv 2506.15792), confirmed through Crossref metadata, the DOI resolver and the citation message in chemprop's CheMeleon loader; the ACS landing page returns 403 to automated fetch, so the journal full text was not read. Description corrected from RDKit to Mordred descriptors per the arXiv v2 methods (1,613 Mordred descriptors on 1M PubChem molecules). MIT on the repository and on the Zenodo weights record; concept record 15426600 resolves to version 15460715, the file chemprop downloads. Year kept as 2025 (arXiv first posted 2025-06-18).

name: MarinDNA
description: Nucleotide-level causal DNA language model family from Open Athena trained on curated vertebrate genome regions, comprising a 1.12B-parameter flagship and an eight-model 46M-4B scaling ladder.
status: Open code + weights (Apache-2.0), ungated; documented by an official release write-up rather than a paper
io: DNA sequence (256-token context) -> nucleotide likelihoods, embeddings and variant-effect scores
use_cases: Zero-shot variant-effect prediction, genomic representation learning, DNA model scaling research
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_3.json. Apache-2.0 on code and weights; no preprint or DOI exists, so the official blog release is the primary document.

name: CENO
description: Long-context autoregressive DNA foundation model family from Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory built on a Mamba, sparse-attention and mixture-of-experts hybrid backbone at 80M-1B parameters, with CENO-P variants post-trained on multi-species alignments for variant-effect scoring.
status: Open code + 15 checkpoints (Apache-2.0), ungated; documented by a self-hosted technical report with no DOI
io: DNA sequence with contexts up to about one million tokens -> likelihoods, embeddings, variant-effect scores or generated DNA
use_cases: Variant-effect prediction, long-context genome modelling, regulatory sequence design, embedding extraction
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_3.json. Apache-2.0 on code and weights, LICENSE and NOTICE present in the weight repositories.

name: LDARNet
description: Hierarchical genomic representation model with learnable tokenization: dynamic chunking learns content-aware token boundaries, a bidirectional BiMamba-2 backbone processes the compressed sequence, and dechunking restores base resolution.
status: Open code + 2M and 110M weights (Apache-2.0), ungated; checkpoints load through the project's own loader
io: DNA sequence -> learned token boundaries, nucleotide and sequence embeddings, masked-token predictions
use_cases: Genomic representation learning, regulatory and histone-mark classification, tokenization research
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_3.json. Apache-2.0 declared on the repository and both model cards.

name: Carbon (Carbon-500M / 3B / 8B)
description: Family of open autoregressive genomic foundation models at 500M, 3B and 8B parameters from Hugging Face Biology with partners, pretrained on about one trillion 6-mer tokens with a 32,768-token native context extendable through YaRN.
status: Open code + weights (Apache-2.0), ungated; documented by an official technical report with no DOI
io: DNA or RNA sequence as 6-mer tokens with optional metadata tokens -> generated sequence and token likelihoods for zero-shot variant scoring
use_cases: Genomic sequence generation and recovery, zero-shot variant-effect prediction, long-context genomic retrieval
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_4.json. Apache-2.0 on code and all three checkpoints, no gating.

name: ModernGENA (base / large)
description: DNA foundation model from AIRI that adapts the ModernBERT encoder to genomic sequence modelling, released as base and large checkpoints pretrained by masked language modelling on 443 vertebrate genome assemblies with the GENA-LM BPE vocabulary.
status: Public ungated weights with no licence stated on either model card; release and fine-tuning code under MIT
io: DNA sequence tokenized with the GENA-LM BPE vocabulary -> contextual embeddings and masked-token predictions
use_cases: Nucleotide Transformer benchmark tasks, sequence classification, per-token regression on signal tracks
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_4.json. Neither weight repository declares a licence; only the code repository is MIT, so checkpoint reuse terms are unresolved.

name: BOTANIC-0 (Botanic0-S / -M / -L)
description: Family of plant genomic foundation models from Living Models spanning about 100M to 1B parameters, pretrained by masked language modelling on nuclear DNA from 43 phylogenetically diverse plant genomes.
status: Weights behind an automatic contact-sharing gate under a custom research-only, non-commercial licence
io: Plant DNA sequence as 6-mer tokens -> contextual embeddings and masked-token predictions for zero-shot scoring and fine-tuning
use_cases: Regulatory element annotation, gene expression inference, variant effect prediction, crop genotype-to-phenotype modelling
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_4.json. Custom livingmodels-research licence is research-use only and all three repositories are auto-gated.

name: MKB (Monkey King Bang)
description: Unified scientific multimodal model from the Shanghai Academy of AI for Science that wraps native scientific encoders and decoders around a shared vision-language backbone (about 11.7B parameters), covering protein, RNA, DNA, molecule, weather, medical-image and text modalities through one natural-language interface.
status: Public ungated weights under a composite licence: Apache-2.0 for code and all weights except the SAM 3 medical-image branch, which follows Meta's SAM License
io: Natural-language prompt plus a sequence, molecule, gridded weather field or medical image -> answers, generated RNA or SMILES, forecasts or segmentation masks
use_cases: Cross-modal scientific question answering, sequence understanding, text-to-molecule and RNA design, medical-image segmentation
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_4.json. Composite terms: the SAM 3 branch carries Meta's SAM License with acceptable-use restrictions; the card shows gating text while the hub API reports the repository as ungated.

name: MGM2
description: Multimodal microbiome foundation model pretrained on 1,821,291 MicrobeAtlas samples and 225,067 OTUs, coupling sequence embeddings with relative-abundance conditioning and community-semantic alignment; released in four scales.
status: Public ungated code and four checkpoints, but no licence is declared for either code or weights
io: OTU/ASV abundance table with optional representative sequences -> microbial token embeddings and a community-level embedding
use_cases: Biome classification, faecal microbiota transplantation response and post-transplant composition prediction, drug-perturbation response prediction when paired with Uni-Mol molecular representations
audit_note: Re-checked 2026-10-10. bioRxiv v2 (2026-09-30) is retitled 'MGM2 as a Multimodal Foundation Model for Microbial Community States and Responses' and adds drug-perturbation prediction via task-specific heads on frozen MGM2 states plus Uni-Mol; sample descriptions remain a pretraining alignment target (as in v1), not an inference input. v1 reported wastewater forecasting across 24 plants; v2 drops it, though repository scripts remain. GitHub has no LICENSE file and the Hugging Face card declares no licence, so reuse rights are not granted; the preprint (v1 and v2) is CC BY-NC 4.0. Limits: preprint, not peer reviewed; repository and checkpoints last updated 2026-07-15, before v2.

name: NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit
description: NVIDIA toolkit that packages its life-science model and library stack as agent-callable skills, so an agent can select, run and interpret bio foundation models across single tasks and multi-step workflows.
status: Open source (Apache-2.0 code, CC BY 4.0 skills and docs); underlying models keep their own licences and hosted endpoints need an NVIDIA API key
io: Agent skill invocation with biological inputs -> outputs of the underlying BioNeMo models with interpretation guidance
use_cases: Structure prediction, docking, generative chemistry, protein and binder design, genomics analysis, agentic discovery workflows
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_7.json. Dual Apache-2.0 OR CC-BY-4.0 licence quoted from the repository LICENSE; distinct from the existing NVIDIA BioNeMo framework record.

name: Boltz Lab / Boltz API
description: Hosted platform and API from Boltz PBC serving the company's biomolecular models with managed compute: BoltzMol-1 for small-molecule hit discovery and BoltzProt-1 for protein design, alongside the open Boltz model lineage.
status: Commercial hosted service with a self-serve free tier, then usage-based pricing; hosted models have no public weights, while Boltz-2 and BoltzGen remain open source
io: Target, ligands and job specification through the web interface or SDK -> designed molecules or binders with predicted structure, affinity and ADME properties
use_cases: Small-molecule hit discovery, de novo protein and nanobody design, structure and affinity prediction, agentic discovery pipelines
audit_note: Re-verified 2026-10-10: boltz.bio pages now 301-redirect to boltz.com; platform/API links and sources updated to boltz.com. Model roles, SDK, usage-based pricing and free monthly allowance (stated on the Boltz Lab pricing page) re-checked on first-party boltz.com pages; github.com/jwohlwend/boltz confirmed MIT via GitHub API. Limits: hosted-only status of BoltzMol-1/BoltzProt-1 rests on homepage labels (Boltz Lab/Boltz API vs Open-source), not an explicit no-weights statement; BoltzGen open-source status from first-party Boltz pages, its repository not checked; technical reports not fetched, so no paper_links.

name: ProtGPT3
description: Open family of autoregressive protein language models from the Ferruz lab spanning 112M to 10B parameters in a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture, with DPO-aligned variants and an MSA-promptable model for homolog-conditioned generation.
status: Seven ungated checkpoints on Hugging Face described as open source in the paper, but no licence is declared on the model cards or code repository
io: Amino-acid prefix with a direction token, or a prompt of homologous sequences -> generated protein sequences and per-sequence likelihoods
use_cases: De novo protein generation, family-conditioned and homolog-prompted design, zero-shot variant scoring, enzyme design
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_8.json. No SPDX licence exists on any of the seven model cards or in the code repository; the only availability statement is the paper's appendix.

name: MSA Pairformer
description: 111M-parameter MSA-based protein language model that adapts AlphaFold's Pairformer sequence-pair updates into a pretrained model of protein and protein-protein coevolution, published in Cell after a 2025 preprint and weight release.
status: Open code + weights under a modified MIT licence that explicitly permits commercial use, ungated
io: Query sequence plus its multiple sequence alignment -> sequence and pairwise embeddings, contact maps and zero-shot variant scores
use_cases: Protein embedding, unsupervised and interface contact prediction, interacting-pair screening, variant-effect prediction
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_8.json. Modified MIT licence covers code and weights and states commercial use is permitted.

name: ProLLaMA
description: Llama-2-7B-based multitask protein language model trained by continued pretraining on protein sequences followed by instruction tuning, handling both superfamily-conditioned generation and protein understanding tasks.
status: Public ungated weights and Apache-2.0 code; the checkpoints derive from Llama-2-7B and the cards direct users to the Llama 2 licence
io: Instruction such as generate-by-superfamily or determine-superfamily, optionally with an amino-acid prefix -> generated sequence or predicted superfamily
use_cases: Controllable protein generation by superfamily, prefix-conditioned generation, superfamily prediction, instruction-style protein tasks
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_8.json. Cards declare apache-2.0 but also instruct users to follow the Llama 2 licence for the derived weights, so reuse is constrained by the base-model terms.

name: UTRGen
description: Unified 5' UTR modelling framework built on a small autoregressive decoder pretrained on multi-species 5' UTR sequence and adapted through lightweight heads to translation efficiency, expression, ribosome load and IRES tasks, with reinforcement-learning-guided design.
status: Open MIT code; pretrained checkpoints distributed as a publicly shared Google Drive archive with no separate terms
io: Nucleotide prompt or 5' UTR sequence -> generated UTRs, or predicted translation efficiency, expression, ribosome load and IRES class
use_cases: 5' UTR generation and design, translation efficiency and expression prediction, IRES identification
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_8.json. The Drive folder is world-readable and lists the checkpoint archive, but its contents were not opened and Drive is not a permanent archive.

name: Shifu-LMR
description: Family of compact masked-language-model RNA backbones released as the model component of the Shifu framework, spanning 65M to 290M parameters including a 4,096-token long-context variant, alongside a leakage-audited corpus and evaluation protocol.
status: Open code + four checkpoints (MIT), ungated; corpus databases retain their own terms
io: RNA nucleotide sequence -> contextual residue embeddings and masked-token predictions for fine-tuning
use_cases: RNA representation learning, secondary-structure prediction after fine-tuning, leakage-free benchmarking, continued pretraining
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_8.json. MIT on the repository and all four weight repositories, none gated.

name: NUMonomer
description: End-to-end model that predicts three-dimensional RNA and single-stranded DNA structures directly from sequence, without MSAs, secondary-structure annotations or language-model features.
status: Open MIT code; pretrained weights distributed through the authors' Google Drive folder
io: RNA or single-stranded DNA sequence -> predicted 3D structure with confidence scores
use_cases: RNA 3D structure prediction, ssDNA structure prediction, large-scale structure modelling
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_9.json. MIT is the only stated grant; the checkpoint file is listed in the public Drive folder but was not downloaded.

name: RNAPro
description: NVIDIA RNA 3D structure prediction model developed with the hosts and winners of a public RNA folding competition, coupling an all-atom co-folding trunk with MSAs, template modelling and the frozen RibonanzaNet2 RNA foundation model.
status: Open code (Apache-2.0) + public weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, ungated
io: RNA sequence with MSAs and templates -> all-atom 3D structure
use_cases: RNA 3D structure prediction, template-based RNA modelling, structure-driven RNA drug discovery
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_9.json. Apache-2.0 code and NVIDIA Open Model License weights, both quoted from official artifacts.

name: RNAElectra
description: Single-nucleotide-resolution RNA language model pretrained on RNAcentral non-coding RNAs with a replaced-token-detection objective rather than masked language modelling, released as a reusable discriminator backbone.
status: Open weights (Apache-2.0), ungated; no separate code repository
io: RNA sequence -> per-nucleotide contextual embeddings for fine-tuning
use_cases: RNA structure and function prediction, RNA-protein and RNA-RNA interaction prediction, modification and stability prediction
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_9.json. Apache-2.0 declared on the model card; the preprint's data-availability statement confirms author ownership of the upload.

name: DGRNA
description: Long-context RNA foundation model built on bidirectional Mamba2 with attention, pretrained on 100 million RNA sequences to avoid the quadratic cost of attention on long RNAs.
status: Open MIT code; pretrained weights distributed through the authors' Google Drive folder
io: RNA sequence -> per-nucleotide contextual embeddings for fine-tuning
use_cases: RNA embedding extraction, RNA structure and function prediction, long RNA modelling
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_9.json. MIT is the only stated grant; the checkpoint filename is listed in the public Drive folder but was not downloaded.

name: RibonanzaNet2
description: Das lab RNA foundation model pretrained to map RNA sequence to per-nucleotide chemical reactivity for DMS and SHAPE probes; the released alpha checkpoint supplies frozen sequence and pairwise features reused by downstream models such as RNAPro.
status: Public MIT-licensed alpha weights on Kaggle and MIT training code; no RibonanzaNet2-specific paper exists
io: RNA sequence -> per-nucleotide DMS and SHAPE reactivity profiles plus sequence and pairwise representations
use_cases: Chemical reactivity prediction, RNA secondary structure prediction, embedding backbone for RNA 3D structure prediction
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_9.json. Weight metadata and the MIT instance licence were read through the Kaggle public API after a parallel lane could not render the HTML page; the release is self-described as an alpha and has no dedicated paper.

name: PerturbGen
description: Generative single-cell model from the Lotfollahi lab trained on over 100 million transcriptomes that predicts perturbation responses along cellular trajectories rather than at a single static state.
status: Open MIT code; the pretraining checkpoint is publicly downloadable and ungated but the model card states no licence
io: Source-state expression + genetic perturbation + target state -> predicted target-state expression, gene embeddings and gene programs
use_cases: Trajectory-aware perturbation prediction, gene-program discovery, in silico genetic screens
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_10.json. Code is MIT; the weights ship without any stated licence.

name: PRISM2
description: Paige multimodal slide-level pathology foundation model coupling a whole-slide Perceiver encoder to a language-model decoder, trained on 2.3 million whole-slide images with report-derived question-answer pairs; released with a survival-finetuned variant.
status: Gated weights (manual approval, institutional email) under CC BY-NC-ND-4.0, non-commercial research only
io: Virchow2 tile embeddings of a whole-slide image + optional text prompt -> slide-level embedding and diagnostic text
use_cases: Slide-level embeddings, cancer detection, diagnostic question answering, biomarker and survival prediction
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_11.json. Successor to the separate PRISM record, whose links were narrowed to PRISM v1 in the same migration; weights are manually gated and non-commercial.

name: KRONOS2
description: Second-generation marker-aware vision foundation model for multiplex spatial proteomics from the Mahmood Lab, pretrained with a 268-marker vocabulary to produce one embedding per multiplexed image patch conditioned on the markers present.
status: Gated weights (manual approval, institutional email) under CC BY-NC-ND-4.0; no dedicated KRONOS2 paper yet, the card cites the KRONOS v1 paper
io: Multiplex spatial proteomics image patch -> 768-dimensional marker-aware patch embedding
use_cases: Cell phenotyping, tissue classification, biomarker discovery, patient stratification from multiplex imaging
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_11.json. Separate release from the existing KRONOS record; a KRONOS2 technical report is announced but not published.

name: GigaPath-Flash
description: Efficient distillations of the Prov-GigaPath pathology foundation model from Microsoft Research: a ViT-S/16 tile encoder with a LongNet slide encoder retaining most slide-level performance at far lower compute, plus the companion GigaTIME-Flash that predicts virtual multiplexed-immunofluorescence maps from H&E tiles.
status: Apache-2.0 weights behind a click-through contact gate; the model cards restrict intended use to research and exclude deployment
io: H&E tiles and whole-slide images -> tile and slide embeddings; H&E tiles -> 23-channel virtual multiplexed-immunofluorescence maps
use_cases: Whole-slide representation learning, slide-level classification and biomarker prediction, tumour microenvironment mapping
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_12.json. Apache-2.0 is the operative licence, but the cards' research-only intended-use text and the access gate are recorded in the status field.

name: TissueFormer
description: Multimodal foundation model from the Uhler lab for paired histopathology and spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution, using linear-complexity whole-slide attention over more than 17 million image-expression pairs.
status: Open MIT code; pretrained checkpoints distributed through Google Drive links in the official repository with no separate terms
io: Histology images with or without paired spatial transcriptomics -> single-cell spatial expression predictions and cell-, region- and slide-level embeddings
use_cases: Spatial gene-expression prediction from H&E, cell- region- and slide-level diagnosis, mechanism hypothesis generation
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_12.json. MIT repository licence is the only grant covering the Drive-hosted checkpoints.

name: CellWorld
description: Joint-embedding predictive foundation model for spatial transcriptomics in which cells are tokens and masked spatial regions are predicted in latent space rather than reconstructed as gene counts; four variants pretrained on 46 million human cells.
status: Open code + weights (MIT), ungated, four scales
io: Spatially resolved single-cell expression with coordinates -> latent cell embeddings, with probe and finetune heads for annotation and niche prediction
use_cases: Spatial transcriptomics representation learning, cell-type annotation, tissue region and niche prediction
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_12.json. MIT on code and weights; the weight repository became public and ungated before verification.

name: SEAL
description: Self-supervised framework from the Mahmood Lab that finetunes existing patch-level pathology foundation models against paired spatial transcriptomics, yielding molecularly aligned drop-in vision encoders with matched expression encoders; CONCH and UNIv2 variants are released.
status: Click-through gated weights under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; the code repository states no licence
io: H&E histology patch -> molecularly aligned patch embedding, with a paired expression encoder for cross-modal retrieval
use_cases: Molecular status and expression prediction, treatment-response assessment, gene-image retrieval, patch- and slide-level tasks
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_13.json. Weights are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and gated; the GitHub repository has no licence file, so code terms are unspecified.

name: SpatialFusion
description: Lightweight multimodal model from the Uhler lab that fuses histology and spatial-transcriptomics embeddings from pretrained backbones into joint neighbourhood representations and pathway-informed spatial niches at single-cell resolution.
status: Open source (MIT) with pretrained checkpoints for each backbone combination bundled in the package
io: Paired histology and spatial transcriptomics embeddings -> joint neighbourhood embedding and pathway-informed niche assignments
use_cases: Spatial niche mapping, multimodal spatial embedding, tumour microenvironment characterization, cohort finetuning
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_13.json. MIT covers code and the bundled checkpoints; the fusion heads are small modules over frozen third-party encoders.

name: Path Foundation
description: Google Health AI histopathology embedding model: a ViT-S trained with masked siamese networks on 60 million H&E patches from public tumour studies at three magnifications, producing 384-dimensional patch embeddings.
status: Weights gated by click-through acceptance of Google's Health AI Developer Foundations terms; commercial use permitted subject to those use restrictions
io: H&E histopathology patch -> 384-dimensional embedding
use_cases: Tumour identification and grading, biomarker detection, similar-image search, data-efficient pathology classifiers
audit_note: Added in the 2026-08-13 delegated discovery refresh; paper or official release document, artifact ownership, and exact licence/access wording verified from primary sources in evidence/additions-2026-08-13/fm_result_13.json. Custom Health AI Developer Foundations terms with use restrictions and a click-through gate; Google documents it as an older single-modality model.

name: ChemBERTa-3
description: Open training and benchmarking framework for chemical foundation models, published in Digital Discovery, with released c3 checkpoints (a 1.1B c3-MoLFormer and a 100M ChemBERTa MLM) on the DeepChem model hub.
status: Open framework + released checkpoints (MIT); two smaller c3-MoLFormer repositories are still weight-free
io: SMILES -> embeddings/task heads
use_cases: Re-training and benchmarking chemical encoders, molecular property prediction, chemical model fine-tuning
audit_note: Promoted from the under-review register on 2026-08-13: the published Digital Discovery article (10.1039/D5DD00348B) confirms the training-framework scope and MIT covers both the framework and the released checkpoints. Evidence: evidence/hold-review-2026-08-13/fm_hold_review_4.json.

name: Virchow / Virchow2 (and Virchow2G)
description: Paige/MSK self-supervised ViT-H tile-level pathology foundation models: Virchow (632M parameters, 1.5M WSIs), Virchow2 (3.1M+ WSIs) and the 1.85B-parameter Virchow2G, which has no public weights.
io: H&E histology tile -> tile-level embedding (frozen or fine-tuned feature extractor)
status: Member-specific terms: Virchow is Apache-2.0 behind an automatic gate, Virchow2 is CC BY-NC-ND-4.0 non-commercial behind an automatic gate, and Virchow2G is commercial-licence-only with no public weights
use_cases: Tile/slide-level cancer detection, rare cancer detection, biomarker prediction, pan-cancer downstream tasks
audit_note: Promoted from the under-review register on 2026-08-13 with member-specific terms encoded: Virchow Apache-2.0 (auto-gated), Virchow2 CC BY-NC-ND-4.0 (auto-gated, non-commercial), Virchow2G and Virchow2G-Mini commercial licence only with no public artifact and no verified paper. Record-level noncommercial is therefore true. Evidence: evidence/hold-review-2026-08-13/fm_hold_review_3.json.

name: H-optimus-0 / H-optimus-1
description: Bioptimus 1.1B-parameter ViT pathology foundation models trained by self-supervised learning on hundreds of millions of tiles from 500k+ (H-optimus-0) to 1M+ (H-optimus-1) H&E slides; neither model has a peer-reviewed paper or preprint.
io: H&E histology tile -> tile-level feature embedding
status: Member-specific terms: H-optimus-0 is Apache-2.0 behind an automatic gate, H-optimus-1 is CC BY-NC-ND-4.0 behind manual approval with an institutional email
use_cases: Mutation prediction, survival analysis, tissue/cancer classification, biomarker prediction, WSI feature-extraction backbone
audit_note: Promoted from the under-review register on 2026-08-13 with both model cards verified and per-member terms encoded: H-optimus-0 Apache-2.0 (auto-gated), H-optimus-1 CC BY-NC-ND-4.0 (manually gated). The listed paper is a company announcement and is labelled as such; no DOI exists. Evidence: evidence/hold-review-2026-08-13/fm_hold_review_3.json.

name: RIBOSPAN
description: Bidirectional RNA language-model family pretrained at single-nucleotide resolution, with 1,024- and 10,240-nucleotide contexts. The paper evaluates transferable representations, transcript-property prediction, mutation scoring, and a separate conditioned mRNA-generation framework.
status: Apache-2.0 code; custom noncommercial weights and output-use terms. 1K-15/1K-40 ungated; 10K-15 requires approval; 10K-40 not released.
io: RNA sequence -> nucleotide probabilities and embeddings; downstream biological predictions
use_cases: RNA representation learning, mutation-effect scoring, full-transcript property prediction; paper also studies mRNA design
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. The family landing repository itself contains documentation, not weights. Weight files are listed in the separately linked checkpoint repositories. Custom commercial-use restrictions also cover outputs and output-derived models; this is not a standard CC noncommercial licence. No gated checkpoint was downloaded.

name: Monroe
description: Molecular graph encoder pretrained on quantum-chemical properties, bioassay targets, and conformer denoising. Frozen molecular embeddings support downstream prediction with a separate prior-data-fitted model.
status: MIT code and released encoder weights via Git LFS; reported TabPFN v3 downstream prediction requires separate licence acceptance and access.
io: SMILES/featurized molecular graph -> 720-dimensional embedding; embeddings plus labelled examples -> downstream predictions through a separate predictor
use_cases: Low-data molecular-property prediction, ADMET modelling, bioassay prediction, activity-cliff evaluation
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. The released checkpoint directory and LFS pointer were inspected; weights were not downloaded or executed. MIT for the encoder does not establish the terms of TabPFN.

name: NucleicBERT
description: Masked RNA language model pretrained on approximately 30 million noncoding RNA sequences, learning single-sequence representations for structural and functional tasks without requiring a multiple-sequence alignment.
status: Open code + weights (Apache-2.0); public pretrained/task checkpoints on Zenodo.
io: Single RNA sequence -> embeddings; task heads -> secondary structure, contact maps, splice-site or fitness predictions
use_cases: RNA representation learning, structure and contact prediction, splice-site prediction, mutation-fitness analysis
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. Journal full-text sections were inspected through web retrieval; direct HTTP returned a JavaScript challenge. Zenodo lists pretrained.pt and separate task checkpoints under Apache-2.0. The archive was first published in 2025; the journal article is from September 2026.

name: GPN-Star
description: Phylogeny-aware genomic language model using whole-genome alignments and species-tree information to learn evolutionary constraints. Human checkpoints cover vertebrate, mammalian, and primate alignments.
status: Open code + weights (MIT); public human checkpoints; aligned genomic input is required for training and inference.
io: Whole-genome alignment with species context -> nucleotide probabilities, embeddings and variant-effect scores
use_cases: Genome-wide variant scoring, evolutionary-constraint analysis, prioritization of coding and noncoding variants
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. Separate from GPN-MSA and PhyloGPN. Human model cards and safetensors listings were checked; no all-family licence claim is made for the separately distributed datasets or other species. Year follows the verified September 2025 preprint, not the 2026 journal publication.

name: Mol-JEPA
description: Joint-embedding predictive model learning molecular representations from complementary chemical and biological modalities, including cellular effects, binding affinity, ADMET properties and quantum-chemical information.
status: Open code + weights (CC BY-NC 4.0); public weights and custom inference code on Hugging Face.
io: SMILES -> molecular embeddings; embeddings support downstream property predictors
use_cases: Molecular representation learning, ADMET prediction, low-data property modelling, integration of biochemical context
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. Official corporate repository directly links the author model-hub account, resolving ownership. Model API lists model.safetensors. The README explicitly applies CC BY-NC 4.0 to code as well as weights.

name: MicroGenomer
description: Microbial genome language model trained hierarchically on genomic sequences and marker genes to produce gene- and genome-level representations and support ecophysiological trait prediction.
status: Open code + weights (MIT); official repository links the public author-hosted 470M checkpoint.
io: Genome-labelled coding DNA sequences in CSV -> genomic embeddings and task-specific trait predictions
use_cases: Microbial genome representation, growth-rate and environmental-trait prediction, comparative microbial genomics
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. Resolves the previous unnamed watchlist lead. The official BGI repository links the model account; model_states.pt and downstream files are listed, with MIT in the model metadata. The paper is a December 2025 preprint.

name: LAMBDA (prophage benchmark)
description: Benchmark for genomic language-model embeddings using phage/bacterial discrimination, fine-tuning, diagnostic tests, and genome-wide prophage detection, with reusable datasets and result visualization.
status: MIT evaluation code; CC BY 4.0 Zenodo dataset/results/probe archive; upstream foundation-model weights retain their own terms. Non-EVO2 fine-tuned task checkpoints are author-request-only.
io: DNA segments or bacterial genomes plus model embeddings/predictions -> prophage-detection and representation-evaluation metrics
use_cases: Genomic-model comparison, probing and fine-tuning assessment, prophage-detection evaluation
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. The full-text source inspected is the March 2026 preprint; September journal identity was verified from publisher metadata/search while full publisher access was restricted. The small checkpoint archive contains probe heads, not redistributed EVO2 foundation weights. The README separately makes non-EVO2 fine-tuned task checkpoints available only on author request; the public benchmark archive is not an all-checkpoint release.

name: KinConfBench
description: Curated benchmark of 2,225 human kinase chains assessing whether cofolding models recover ligand-dependent kinase conformations, with geometric and conformation-state evaluation.
status: UC Regents software terms permit educational, research and not-for-profit use; precomputed inference archive is CC BY 4.0.
io: Kinase structures and cofolding outputs -> conformation-state, geometric and diversity metrics
use_cases: Cofolding-model evaluation, kinase conformation benchmarking, ligand-induced structural-change assessment
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. Named reusable benchmark, not a new foundation-model checkpoint. Publisher full-text sections, UC Regents licence body and Figshare file metadata were inspected. Dataset archive was not downloaded.

name: PlantRNA-FM
description: Plant RNA foundation model pretrained on RNA sequences from 1,124 species, supporting interpretable representations and identification of functional sequence and structural motifs.
status: Model hub; MIT model and public safetensors weights; inference uses the released model card and standard Transformers.
io: Plant RNA sequence -> base-model embeddings; task-specific predictions require downstream fine-tuning
use_cases: Plant RNA function, genic-region annotation, translation-related motif analysis
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. Promoted by splitting the original family; the original stable ID follows PlantRNA-FM. Residual mRNA-FM remains held under bfm-mrna-fm. The prior combined name is retained as a historical alias, not a claim that the terms apply to mRNA-FM. The public model card demonstrates base embeddings; paper genic-region/translation predictions use task-specific fine-tuning.

name: MultiFlow
description: Pretrained joint sequence-and-structure generative model combining discrete and continuous flows, with unconditional protein co-design, inverse folding and forward folding modes.
status: Open code + weights (MIT implementation; CC BY 4.0 Zenodo weights/datasets), public.
io: Optional protein sequence or backbone structure -> generated sequence/structure pair, inverse-folded sequence or predicted backbone
use_cases: Protein co-design, inverse folding, forward folding
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. Original family stable ID is retained by MultiFlow. FrameFlow is separate; FrameDiff remains held. Distinct inference modes establish reusable scope; archive licensing is CC BY 4.0, not the code repository MIT licence.

name: FrameFlow
description: SE(3) flow-matching model with released pretrained checkpoints for unconditional protein-backbone generation and conditional motif scaffolding.
status: Open code + weights (MIT code; CC BY 4.0 Zenodo weights/datasets); generated structures have not been experimentally validated by the repository authors.
io: Requested length or fixed structural motif -> sampled protein backbones and scaffold candidates
use_cases: De novo backbone generation, motif-conditioned scaffold design
audit_note: Evidence and access reviewed 2026-09-11; see evidence/refresh-2026-09-11/candidate_decisions.json. Split from the held three-member family. Both unconditional and motif-scaffolding inference paths are documented; the scientific-use caveat is kept separate from licence terms.

name: HybriDNA
description: Decoder-only hybrid Transformer–Mamba2 DNA language model in 300M, 3B and 7B variants that processes sequences up to about 131 kb at single-nucleotide resolution for both understanding and generation tasks.
status: Ungated weights (300M, 3B, 7B) with Apache-2.0 model-hub metadata, released by the first author on a personal account; the first-author GitHub companion is a usage README that states Apache 2.0 but has no LICENSE file; model code is also published in the GO-CRE repository under MIT (LICENSE file); no Microsoft organisation release.
io: DNA sequence (up to ~131 kb) -> embeddings, sequence likelihoods and generated DNA; fine-tuned sequence classification
use_cases: Short- and long-range DNA understanding (BEND, GUE and LRB tasks), synthetic cis-regulatory element generation, sequence embedding and fine-tuning
audit_note: Promoted from HOLD on 2026-10-10. What changed: author-controlled links now connect the paper to the weights. The GitHub account Mamingqian maintained the arXiv-linked project page, serves the first author's personal site and owns Mamingqian/HybriDNA, which lists the three Mishamq Hugging Face checkpoints. Hugging Face Papers shows the first author's authorship of arXiv 2502.10807 claimed and verified by the Mishamq account. The GO-CRE preprint (bioRxiv 2026, co-authored by HybriDNA authors including Microsoft Research co-authors) names the GO-CRE repository as the HybriDNA implementation, and that repository calls the Mishamq checkpoints the published checkpoints. Hub configs match the layer and hidden-size table in arXiv v2; hub parameter counts are about 297.5M, 3.12B and 6.25B, so the paper's 7B variant holds about 6.3B parameters. Limits: a personal first-author release, not a Microsoft organisation release (the project page's microsoft/HybriDNA link is 404), and institutional authorisation is not documented. That the uploads are the exact paper checkpoints rests on the authors' statements. The 3B card text is copied from the 300M card, though its config is correct. Apache-2.0 for the weights appears in hub metadata, cards and the first-author README (badge and License section); none of these repositories has a LICENSE file. The GO-CRE copy of the model code is MIT. Inference needs Hugging Face remote code plus mamba-ssm and flash-attn. Evidence: October 2026 hold re-review, batch 1, with adversarial verification.

name: RCLM (DRfold2 RNA language model)
description: Evoformer-style RNA language model (about 47.5M parameters) pretrained on about 30 million RNAcentral sequences with a masked composite-likelihood objective. From a single sequence it produces per-residue and pairwise embeddings. It is the pretrained module of the DRfold2 ab initio RNA 3D structure predictor and is also released as a standalone embedding package.
status: Open MIT code (RCLM repository LICENSE file). The pretrained RCLM checkpoint (about 190 MB) is a public Google Drive file linked from the official README and lab page, with no stated weight licence. DRfold2 code has MIT text in its README but no LICENSE file; its Zenodo archive is labelled CC BY 4.0. Its 1.3 GB lab-server weight bundle, which also holds the RCLM checkpoint, has no separate terms.
io: Single RNA sequence -> per-residue (L x 512) and pairwise (L x L x 128) embeddings; DRfold2 uses them to predict 3D structure
use_cases: Single-sequence RNA representation and pair-feature extraction; unsupervised contact signal (shown in the DRfold2 paper, extraction code not in the standalone package); input features for RNA 3D structure prediction (DRfold2)
audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10 (October hold review, batch 2; adversarial check passed with corrections). The record is reframed from the DRfold/DRfold2 structure-predictor entry to RCLM, the pretrained language-model component. This meets the recorded reconsider_when branch 'reframing around an evidenced reusable pretrained component'. The official standalone repository leeyang/RCLM (created 2026-07-28 by first author Yang Li, MIT LICENSE, documented embedding API) is linked from the Zhang lab RCLM page. Its rclm/Model.py matches DRfold2's RNALM2/Model.py except for the import line, and DRfold2 loads a checkpoint of the same name (model_hub/RCLM/epoch_67000). Parameter count, training corpus and batch count match the PLOS Biology methods. Limits: the checkpoint is served from a README-linked Google Drive file, not from GitHub files or releases, and no weight licence is stated. The lab page says the checkpoint is in the repository or its Releases page; neither holds it. The method is described only inside the DRfold2 paper (no RCLM-specific paper found in Europe PMC or arXiv). Developers suggest reuse beyond structure tasks; this is not benchmarked, and no third-party reuse of RCLM embeddings was found. The repository is young (five commits on one day, no releases). Inference was not run and no checkpoint was downloaded. DRfold (2023) contains no RCLM and is split off as a residual hold. 'DRfold' is kept as a historical alias for ID continuity only.

name: mRNA-FM
description: Codon-tokenized extension of RNA-FM released by the RNA-FM developers: a 12-layer BERT-style encoder (1,280 hidden dimensions, about 239M parameters) pretrained on about 45 million mRNA coding sequences to produce mRNA embeddings.

paper_links.label: RNA-FM preprint (family citation; no mRNA-FM section)

status: Open code + weights: MIT code (GitHub); mRNA-FM_pretrained.pth sits in the developers' ungated Hugging Face repository, whose card declares Apache-2.0 (the repository has no separate licence file). Third-party Hugging Face conversions carry their own terms (AGPL-3.0 or MIT) and are not the official artifact.
io: Codon-aligned mRNA coding sequence -> codon-level embeddings; downstream heads (e.g. expression prediction)
use_cases: mRNA/CDS representation learning, mRNA expression modelling (official tutorial), coding-sequence analysis
audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10 (October hold review, batch 2, with adversarial re-check). The original artifact is now verified. The official ml4bio/RNA-FM repository (MIT) documents mRNA-FM (45M CDS, 12 layers / 1280 hidden, 239M parameters, codon tokenization). Its loader was first committed as cds_fm_t12 on 2024-03-19 and renamed fm.pretrained.mrna_fm_t12() on 2024-03-21; an official mRNA-expression tutorial uses it. The README points to the developers' Hugging Face repository cuhkaih/rnafm, which lists mRNA-FM_pretrained.pth (957 MB, ungated; card licence Apache-2.0, no licence file). The previously cited yangheng/mrnafm and multimolecule/mrnafm are self-declared unofficial AGPL-3.0 conversions, and Taykhoom/mRNA-FM is a further third-party conversion with an MIT card; none is linked. Limits: there is no mRNA-FM-specific paper. The developers cite the 2022 RNA-FM preprint, whose full text does not mention mRNA-FM or the 45M-CDS corpus, so corpus and size figures rest on developer documentation. Code is MIT on GitHub while the weight hub declares Apache-2.0. The CUHK server download URL in the loader returned 403 to a header request. No checkpoint was downloaded or run. Year 2024 = first public loader commit in the official repository.

name: NeuralPLexer
description: Multiscale deep generative model that predicts protein-ligand complex structures, including ligand-induced conformational changes, directly from protein sequence and ligand molecular graph. A diffusion process with biophysical constraints samples residue-level contact maps and then all heavy-atom coordinates.
io: Protein sequence(s) or PDB + ligand SMILES/SDF (none, one or several ligands), optional template structure -> sampled protein-ligand complex conformations (PDB/SDF) ranked by predicted confidence
status: Open code (BSD-3-Clause-Clear) + public pretrained checkpoints, evaluation datasets and predictions in one open Zenodo archive; the README limits this archive to non-commercial use under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (the Zenodo record lists no licence)
use_cases: Protein-ligand co-folding and blind docking, ligand-induced conformational change and apo/holo ensemble modelling, structure-based drug design, enzyme engineering
audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-10-10 and promoted by splitting the original v1/NP3 family; the original stable ID follows NeuralPLexer v1, as with the September PlantRNA-FM split. The residual NeuralPLexer3 stays held (proposed ID bfm-neuralplexer3) because Iambic has released no NP3 code, weights or public access route. The prior combined name is kept as a historical alias, not a claim that v1 terms apply to NP3. Limits: the checkpoints are bundled in one 8.9 GB Zenodo zip together with datasets and predictions; the archive was not downloaded, but Zenodo's file-container API confirms models/complex_structure_prediction.ckpt, the checkpoint the README CLI uses. The Zenodo record has no licence field, so the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms for checkpoints and data come from the official README; the paper's Code Ocean capsule (doi 10.24433/CO.9870737.v1) lists a custom software licence plus CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in DataCite. The code has one 2024 release, and its last commit was 2025-10-06. Year corrected from 2024 to 2022 (arXiv v1, 2022-09-30).

name: Tabula
description: Privacy-preserving single-cell foundation model pretrained with federated learning across eight tissue clients (15 million cells), combining gene-wise reconstruction and cell-wise contrastive objectives over a tabular cell-by-gene representation.

code_links.label: Pretrained checkpoints (Google Drive, linked from tutorials)

status: Code under a custom non-commercial licence, pretraining code not yet released; eight pretrained tissue-client checkpoints sit in a public Google Drive folder linked from the official tutorials, viewable without sign-in; no licence stated for the weights (all rights reserved by default)
io: scRNA-seq expression (tabular cell x gene) -> cell/gene embeddings, fine-tuned task predictions (annotation, integration, perturbation, GRN inference)
use_cases: Cell type annotation, batch and multi-omics integration, imputation, perturbation prediction, zero-shot gene-regulation inference, aging/rejuvenation factor prioritization, privacy-preserving federated pretraining
audit_note: Promoted 2026-10-10 from HOLD (condition: official reusable pretrained checkpoint released and terms verified). Earlier reviews checked only the main README and release metadata. The official tutorials README points to the notebooks for weights, and five tutorial notebooks (annotation, integration, GRN inference, perturbation, reverse perturbation) link one public Google Drive folder, present in the annotation notebook since its first commit (2025-03-03). The folder lists eight tissue-client checkpoints (blood, brain, heart, intestine, kidney, lung, others, pancreas; 51.2 MB each, modified 2025-01-08), matching the paper's eight federated clients. The repository also ships fine-tuning code, a tokenizer and vocab.json. Terms: the repository's custom non-commercial licence covers the software; the weights state no licence of their own. Limits: cloud-drive hosting with no published checksums; checkpoints were not downloaded or loaded; pretraining code is withheld; the loader falls back to partial weight loading on a mismatch; the Chiron Model Hub route needs a Hypha token and was not inspected.

name: RudolfV 2
description: Aignostics family of pathology vision foundation models: RudolfV 2 is a ViT-g/8 tile-level feature extractor (1.1B parameters) trained on more than 300k de-identified whole-slide images from Charité and LMU Munich archives, released with distilled ViT-B (86M) and ViT-S (22M) variants.
status: Gated weights for all three models (manual approval; academic or non-profit email; granted at Aignostics' discretion) under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 plus controlling supplementary terms: academic research only; no diagnostic, clinical or commercial use; no use to train models that replicate or approximate it, or to provide training signals for any foundation model or general-purpose pathology model. Custom inference code ships inside the gated repositories; the technical report announces weights only, and no public training-code repository or pretraining-data release was found.
io: Pathology image tile (H&E in the card example) -> tile-level CLS embedding plus register and patch tokens (1536-dimensional for RudolfV 2)
use_cases: Tissue and tumor classification, grading, biomarker prediction, slide-level modeling via multiple-instance learning
audit_note: Promoted 2026-10-10 from HOLD (terms). The exact terms and member-level access were read on the public model-card pages of RudolfV 2, 2-B and 2-S; raw card and file endpoints still return 401 without approval. Terms: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 plus supplementary terms that control in case of conflict. All three models are manually gated and require an academic or non-profit email. Limits: weights were not downloaded; the technical report is author-hosted, not peer-reviewed and has no DOI; benchmarks are author-run. Atlas evidence was not used. Evidence: evidence/refresh-2026-10-10/hold_reviews.json.

name: OpenProtein.AI
description: Commercial protein-engineering cloud from NE47 Bio that serves its PoET-2, PoET and proprietary Prot-seq/Rotaprot protein language models alongside community models (ESM, AlphaFold2, Boltz, RFdiffusion) through a web app, REST API and Python client. The self-hostable PoET and PoET-2 models have their own entries.
status: Commercial hosted service (web app, REST API, Python client); accounts via a contact form; products page advertises free academic use (PoET section), subscription tiers have no public prices; proprietary Prot-seq/Rotaprot models are hosted only, with no public weights found; Python client licence text is BSD-3-Clause while package metadata says MIT. Self-hosted PoET/PoET-2 weights are covered by their own entries.
io: Protein sequences, families/MSAs, structures and assay data via web app or API -> embeddings, variant-effect scores, trained property predictors, designed libraries, generated sequences, predicted structures
use_cases: Zero-shot variant-effect prediction, sequence-to-property model training, protein library design, hosted structure prediction and generation
audit_note: Promoted 2026-10-10 by narrowing the held combined record to the OpenProtein.AI platform, which satisfies the recorded condition. Stable-ID disposition: id bfm-openprotein-ai-poet-poet-2 is kept for the platform; the old name moves to aliases; model claims (PoET-2 arXiv 2508.04724, Apache-2.0 code, PoET Non-Commercial weights licence) stay with bfm-poet-2, and PoET stays with bfm-poet; no merge. Platform evidence fetched 2026-10-10: homepage, products page ('Free for academic use!' in the PoET section), Terms & Conditions (operator NE47 Bio, Inc.; no NC clause), sign-up contact form, docs model list including proprietary Prot-seq and Rotaprot models reachable only through the platform, and the Python client (LICENSE.txt BSD-3-Clause text; pyproject/PyPI metadata says MIT; first PyPI release 2023-08-04, so year = earliest verified public access). Limits: no public pricing (/pricing 404); commercial terms not public; API not exercised; PyPI HTML page served a client challenge to automated fetches and was confirmed through the PyPI JSON API. noncommercial kept true because the stated free access route is academic-only; this is a curator call, since the platform terms have no NC clause.

name: JUMP-lite (with Nahual)
description: Compact, analysis-ready subset of the JUMP Cell Painting dataset (655,101 image sites from 551 plates in six sources) with lossless and JPEG XL-compressed image stores, per-site embeddings from DINOv2 (plus a randomly initialised baseline), MorphEm, OpenPhenom and SubCell, Cellpose cell and nuclei masks and perturbation metadata, for benchmarking cell-image representations. Released with Nahual, a framework for deploying representation models reproducibly.
status: MIT harness code (GitHub; Zenodo-archived v1.0/v1.1). Images, Cellpose masks, metadata and per-site embeddings download without credentials from the Cell Painting Gallery, whose gallery-wide licence is CC0 1.0; the release README defers data terms to the gallery and JUMP and has no release-specific licence. Non-commercial terms apply to at least one artifact: the three OpenPhenom embedding variants are outputs of a model under Recursion's Non-Commercial EULA, which requires shared derivatives to carry equivalent terms. CC0 index tables on Zenodo. Nahual has no licence (all rights reserved by default).
io: Compressed Cell Painting images, per-site embeddings and perturbation metadata -> phenotypic-activity and consistency benchmark metrics for cell-image representation methods
use_cases: Benchmarking cell-image representation and foundation models, image-compression sensitivity analysis, morphological-profiling method comparison
audit_note: Promoted 2026-10-10: the recorded condition is met. Unsigned S3 listings return objects for the metadata bundle (7 files), all four image stores, 16 embedding variants, cell/nuclei masks and Target-2 artifacts; an independent spot check of 12 random sites from the release site index (2 per source) returned HTTP 200 for all 252 HEAD requests across the 4 image stores, 16 embedding variants and the MQ cell-mask store. Data licence re-verified: Cell Painting Gallery is CC0 1.0 gallery-wide (AWS Open Data registry); the README defers data terms to the gallery and JUMP. noncommercial set to true because the openphenom-* embedding variants are outputs of OpenPhenom, whose Recursion Non-Commercial EULA (section 7) requires shared Derivative Technology to carry essentially equivalent non-commercial terms; this conflicts with the gallery-wide CC0 label and is unresolved. DINOv2 (Apache-2.0), MorphEm (MIT) and SubCell code (MIT) carry no NC terms. Limits: the documented image and embedding paths (images/2026_jump_lite_v1.0/..., <model>-<codec>/2026_jump_lite_v1.0/) return no objects; the actual paths are images/jump_lite_v1.0/images_compressed/ and <model>-<codec>/jump_lite/v1.0/, so these may still change. The GitHub README and arXiv v3 still say the release awaits gallery promotion. Paper is a preprint (arXiv v3, submitted to WACV 2027). Nahual is described as open-source in the paper but has no licence file, pyproject licence field or PyPI licence. Full object counts were not verified.

name: SABLE
aliases: Structural Antibody Benchmark for deep-Learning Evaluation
description: Versioned structural antibody benchmark and training resource: 16,511 experimental training entries and 3,274 patent-derived AlphaFold3 models (synthetic training entries) paired with 327 manually reviewed, leakage-filtered test entries released after the AlphaFold3 cutoff; each test entry records its nearest training neighbour.
status: Python package and evaluation code MIT; Zenodo v0.2.0 data CC BY 4.0, except the 3,274 patent-derived AlphaFold3 structures, which fall under the AlphaFold3 Output Terms (non-commercial organisations only; may not be used to train AlphaFold3-like structure predictors). Browsable web server, no terms stated.
io: Antibody and antibody-antigen structures + model predictions -> CDR RMSD, DockQ and sequence-recovery metrics, stratifiable by nearest-training-neighbour similarity
use_cases: Evaluating antibody structure prediction and antibody-antigen cofolding models; leakage-aware train/test splits for antibody deep learning
audit_note: Preprint only (bioRxiv v1, 13 Sep 2026). MIT code, CC BY 4.0 data-licence text and AlphaFold3 Output Terms were read; noncommercial flag reflects the AlphaFold3-derived training subset, whose terms also bar training AlphaFold3-like structure predictors. Terms of the NaturalAntibody Patents Database source were not reviewed. The preprint demonstrates evaluation of AlphaFold3, Boltz-1 and OpenDDE as a technical check, not a ranking. Zenodo landing page returns 403 to scripted clients (API 200). Archives were not downloaded.

name: UKBBGym
description: Population-scale benchmark that ranks coding and non-coding variant effect scores by their Spearman correlation with plasma protein abundance and quantitative traits in UK Biobank carriers of ultra-rare variants. A coding-variant, quantitative-trait version rebuilt from public Genebass summary statistics runs locally.
status: Code MIT. Genebass-setup tables labelled CC BY 4.0 on Hugging Face (public, ungated on 2026-10-10, although the repo README still says login is required) and on Zenodo. Embedded third-party scores keep their own terms, including non-commercial terms for CADD and SpliceAI. The primary individual-level benchmark runs only on the UK Biobank RAP under an approved UKB application. The All of Us replication (summary statistics, correlation heatmap only) runs only in the Researcher Workbench. Benchmark only, no model weights.
io: Variant effect scores (e.g. ESM1v, CPT-1, AlphaMissense, GPN-MSA; AlphaGenome AVI and GPN-Star in the Genebass extension) + per-variant carrier phenotype means (UKB) or Genebass effect estimates -> per gene-trait and per-protein Spearman correlations and pairwise method comparisons
use_cases: Comparing protein and DNA language-model variant scores with clinical-label-trained, conservation, splicing and regulatory predictors on observed human phenotypes; scoring a new predictor locally on the Genebass coding-variant setup
audit_note: Preprint only (bioRxiv v1, 2026-10-02; preprint text CC BY-NC-ND). HF API on 2026-10-10: private=false, gated=false, contradicting the repo README's 'private ... login required'. noncommercial=true because the CC BY 4.0-labelled tables redistribute CADD v1.7 scores (non-commercial use free, commercial use needs a licence) and SpliceAI delta scores (Illumina NC terms; inheritance via AbSplice files contested). FM scores are a subset of evaluated predictors. The local Genebass setup covers coding variants and quantitative traits only; protein abundance and non-coding analyses need UKB RAP access. Zenodo HTML returns 403 to scripted clients (API 200). Genebass/UKB summary-statistics terms not checked.

name: ViroBench
description: Benchmark of nucleotide foundation models on viral genomics: 58,314 NCBI viral sequences, 18 classification and generation scenarios with genus-disjoint and temporal splits, and a biosecurity-oriented generation axis; results for more than 60 models on a public leaderboard.
status: CC BY 4.0 benchmark data on Hugging Face (not gated); evaluation code on GitHub has no licence file (all rights reserved by default); public leaderboard, no own model weights. The ViroHyena checkpoints and ViroBlend pretraining data linked from the README are separate Apache-2.0 artifacts, not part of this record.
io: Viral DNA/RNA sequences + nucleotide-model embeddings or generations -> taxonomy/host classification and genome-modelling/CDS-completion metrics
use_cases: Selecting nucleotide foundation models for viral taxonomy and host prediction; generalization under phylogenetic and temporal shift; biosecurity-relevant generation diagnostics
audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-10-10 from primary sources. Older than the October window (arXiv 2026-05-25; ACM KDD '26 proceedings 2026-08-08) but absent from the baseline. The paper and the Hugging Face card cite github.com/QIANJINYDX/ViroBench, which the GitHub API resolves to the authors' own github.com/SII-AGI4S/ViroBench (fork=false, parent=null); that canonical URL is used here.
