Benchmark data CC BY 4.0 and ungated (167 files); evaluation code has no licence file (GitHub licence endpoint 404, no licence blob in the tree), so code reuse is all-rights-reserved; no releases or release assets; leaderboard public, last updated 2026-09-12. The ACM publisher page returns 403 to automated access, so the proceedings identity (container, event, pages 12679-12690, date) comes from Crossref plus the arXiv DOI field; Crossref additionally reports a CC BY 4.0 version-of-record licence that could not be confirmed on the publisher page. The companion artifacts linked from the README were checked and are Apache-2.0 and ungated (YDXX/ViroHyena-436k, -1m, -6m, -253m checkpoints; YDXX/ViroBlend pretraining data), so no non-commercial terms attach to any route; they are separate artifacts and ViroHyena is not covered by this record.

name: HEST-1k
description: Dataset of 1,276 spatial transcriptomics profiles (v1.3.0) paired with H&E whole-slide images across 26 organs and two species, with the HEST-Library Python package and HEST-Benchmark, which tests pathology foundation-model patch encoders on predicting gene expression from morphology across nine cancer tasks.
status: Dataset, library code and benchmark released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (repository README and LICENSE.md). Full HEST-1k data on Hugging Face are gated: login and agreeing to share contact information, approved automatically. HEST-Benchmark data repo is ungated but its hub card declares no licence; terms follow the repository statement. No model weights of its own; benchmarked encoders carry their own, often gated, terms. Non-commercial terms apply.
io: H&E patches (112x112 um at 0.5 um/px) embedded by a frozen pathology encoder -> ridge regression (PCA-256) prediction of 50 highly variable genes; Pearson correlation per task, nine cancer tasks
use_cases: Benchmarking pathology foundation-model encoders on expression prediction from morphology; training and evaluating paired histology-spatial transcriptomics models; biomarker exploration
audit_note: Older (2024) dataset and benchmark absent from the baseline. arXiv reports 1,229 samples; the current README and hub card report 1,276 after versioned additions (v1.2.0, v1.3.0). Benchmark data are fetched by the library from the separate, ungated MahmoodLab/hest-bench repo, which has no hub licence field. Gated files were not downloaded; non-commercial share-alike terms.

name: Runs N' Poses
description: Protein-ligand cofolding benchmark of 2,600 high-resolution systems released after a 30 September 2021 training cutoff, stratified by similarity to training complexes to test whether cofolding models generalize beyond memorisation.
status: Code Apache-2.0; the repo also bundles example AlphaFold 3 outputs under the AlphaFold 3 Output Terms. Zenodo data and predictions are labelled CC BY 4.0, but AlphaFold 3 outputs in them fall under the AlphaFold 3 Output Terms (non-commercial only; no training of AF3-like predictors). ML-ready Polaris copy is CC BY 4.0.
io: Protein sequences, ligand SMILES and MSAs for post-cutoff systems + cofolding predictions -> ligand RMSD, LDDT-PLI and PoseBusters checks stratified by training-set similarity
use_cases: Evaluating AlphaFold3-like cofolding models on post-cutoff ligand complexes; generalization and memorisation analysis
audit_note: Adversarially re-reviewed 2026-10-10. The journal version (NSMB, May 2026) is retitled; it is linked through bioRxiv 'published' metadata, Crossref and its own Data/Code availability sections, which cite the same GitHub repo and Zenodo concept DOI. Publisher full text is not open access and was not read beyond the landing page. The Zenodo CC BY 4.0 label coexists with the AlphaFold 3 Output Terms, as do example AF3 outputs in the Apache-2.0 repo. Polaris dataset page licence checked; no archives downloaded; ModelArchive deposit announced, not checked.

name: Synthetic Genomes Benchmark
description: Model-agnostic benchmark suite comparing DNA from generative genomic models with matched natural genome windows (composition, k-mer spectra, FCGR, nullomers, TFBS, non-B DNA, shallow and deep detectability, context decay), with unpaired population-level variants. A separate Zenodo dataset of paired natural/synthetic windows generated with Evo 2 and megaDNA accompanies it.
status: MIT code (GitHub; Zenodo v1.0.0 archive). Paired-window dataset on Zenodo under MIT. Bundled JASPAR 2026 motif files keep JASPAR's CC BY 4.0 terms. No pretrained detector weights released. External tools (KMC, MEME/FIMO, ZSeeker, G4Hunter, non-B GFA) and the evaluated generator models keep their own terms.
io: Matched natural and model-generated DNA windows (or unpaired natural/synthetic FASTA sets) -> compositional, structural and detectability divergence metrics
use_cases: Evaluating realism of sequences from generative genomic language models; testing decoding and training interventions
audit_note: The journal version (Patterns, Sep 2026) was identified from Crossref metadata only; the publisher page was bot-challenged, so its availability statement was not read. The bioRxiv v2 full text links the GitHub repo and the dataset concept DOI, which resolves to Zenodo record 18826945 (2026-03-01). The title 'Synthetic Genomes Benchmark' comes from the repo, CITATION.cff and Zenodo v1.0.0 (2026-08-20). Only Evo 2 and megaDNA were evaluated; there is no leaderboard. GitHub's licence detector reports NOASSERTION, but LICENSE is the standard MIT text. Several modules need external tools. The paper's environment container (Zenodo 15194473, 'Evo 2 Apptainer') is a third-party deposit and is not part of the suite.

name: BEACON
aliases: Benchmark for Comprehensive RNA Tasks and Language Models
description: RNA benchmark of 13 tasks (about 967k sequences) spanning structural analysis, functional studies and engineering applications. It has unified fine-tuning code for comparing pretrained RNA language models with CNN, ResNet and LSTM baselines, and releases the BEACON-B baseline RNA language model.
status: Code under Apache-2.0. Task data and BEACON-B checkpoints are in public, ungated Google Drive folders with no BEACON-level licence (all rights reserved by default). The paper lists the source-dataset terms. Some components are research-only (tmRDB, SRPDB) or non-commercial (StructImpute, OpenVaccine), and re-hosted third-party model checkpoints keep their own terms.
io: RNA sequences + task labels -> benchmark scores across 13 structural, functional and engineering tasks
use_cases: Comparing RNA foundation models on structure, function and engineering tasks; baseline selection for RNA modelling
audit_note: This 2024 benchmark is absent from the baseline. Source-dataset licences come from paper Appendix A.10 Table 22 (author-stated) and were not re-checked at each upstream source. Several components are research-only or non-commercial, so noncommercial is true. The Drive folders were inspected at listing level only: 13 task folders, and BEACON-B/BEACON-B512 folders containing model.safetensors. Third-party Hugging Face re-uploads exist and are not linked. Repository last pushed 2024-08-02.

name: mRNABench
description: Benchmark suite for mature-mRNA biology that measures the embedding quality of genomic and RNA foundation models on tasks such as half-life, localization, translation efficiency, miRNA targeting and variant effects.
status: Code AGPL-3.0 (GitHub LICENSE; PyPI package mrna-bench). Data: ungated Hugging Face re-hosts of third-party datasets with per-dataset terms: CC BY 4.0 (most), CC BY-SA 4.0 (protein localization), MIT (TraitGym variants); six are marked 'unknown' with no licence grant (eCLIP, MRL Sample, Fazal RNA localization, Ietswaart lifecycle, human and mouse translation efficiency). The repo's own loader says the Fazal source data may not be redistributed. Evaluated models are third-party and download under their own terms.
io: mRNA sequences + frozen model embeddings -> linear-probe scores across mRNA property and function tasks
use_cases: Comparing DNA/RNA foundation models on mRNA half-life, localization, translation and variant tasks
audit_note: Preprint only (bioRxiv v1, 2025-07-08; no journal version found in bioRxiv API or Europe PMC). Data terms checked per Hugging Face dataset card (17 datasets): 10 CC BY 4.0, 1 CC BY-SA 4.0, 1 MIT, 6 'unknown'. Fazal localization data derive from Elsevier-copyrighted supplementary material (PubMed: all rights reserved) and are re-hosted despite the loader's own no-redistribution note. noncommercial=false because no artifact declares NC terms; that is not a permissive-licence claim for the 'unknown' datasets. PyPI latest 1.2.2 lags repo main (V1.3.0 commit, Dec 2025). Upstream licences of original datasets and the paper's new Mamba model not checked.

name: MUBen
description: Benchmark of uncertainty-quantification methods (deterministic, temperature scaling, focal loss, deep ensembles, SWAG, Bayes by Backprop, SGLD, MC dropout) on pretrained molecular backbones (ChemBERTa, GROVER, Uni-Mol, TorchMD-NET) and non-pretrained baselines (RDKit-feature DNN, GIN) across 14 scaffold-split MoleculeNet datasets.
status: Apache-2.0 code (repository LICENSE) with scaffold-split MoleculeNet data files in the repository and no separate data licence; PyPI muben 0.0.2 metadata is inconsistent (licence field MIT, classifier Apache). No MUBen-trained weights; backbone checkpoints are downloaded from upstream projects under their own terms (the default ChemBERTa-77M-MLM hub card states no licence).
io: SMILES (and Uni-Mol conformers) with MoleculeNet labels -> property predictions with uncertainty scored by ROC-AUC/RMSE/MAE, NLL, Brier score, ECE and regression calibration error
use_cases: Comparing calibration of pretrained molecular backbones, selecting UQ methods for molecular property prediction, reliability under scaffold-split distribution shift
audit_note: Benchmark, not a model checkpoint; MUBen releases no weights of its own. MoleculeNet tasks only (14 datasets), four pretrained backbones; repository last pushed April 2024. Repository LICENSE is Apache-2.0, PyPI licence field says MIT while its classifier says Apache. TMLR venue rests on the arXiv comment and README badge; OpenReview returned a bot-challenge page. MoleculeNet source-dataset terms not checked.

name: AtlasFold / AtlasLM
description: Open Atlas model family from KAIST: AtlasLM-3B, a masked protein language model with ESMC-style architecture trained from scratch on about 1.56 billion UniRef, MGnify and MetaClust sequences, plus AtlasFold and AtlasFold-M, which predict all-atom monomer and protein-complex structures from single sequences without an MSA search; protein chains only, no ligands or nucleic acids.
status: Open code + weights (MIT): AtlasLM-3B, AtlasFold and AtlasFold-M weights ungated on Hugging Face; deprecated AtlasLM-600M behind manual access approval; stage checkpoints and structural training data on Google Drive, declared MIT but upstream PDB/MGnify/AlphaFold terms may apply; AtlasLM pretraining pipeline not released
io: Protein sequence(s) or FASTA records (chains separated by ':' for complexes) -> AtlasLM embeddings, hidden states and attention maps, or sampled all-atom monomer/complex structures (PDB/mmCIF) with pLDDT, pTM and, for complexes, ipTM
use_cases: Protein sequence representation, MSA-free monomer structure prediction, protein-protein and antibody-antigen complex structure prediction, retraining or fine-tuning AtlasFold/AtlasFold-M from released stage checkpoints
audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-10-10: bioRxiv record and full text (v1 and v2 posted 2026-09-07; paper links the repository), MIT repository (LICENSE, README licence section, docs/training.md, docs/data.md) and Hugging Face API metadata for all four checkpoints (three ungated with weight files listed; AtlasLM-600M gated='manual'). AtlasLM was trained from scratch (paper A.2.1); its code cites evolutionaryscale/esm, now Biohub/esm under MIT. Weights sit on the first author's personal hub account, linked from the paper's repository. The AtlasLM pretraining pipeline and PLM corpus are not released; released structural datasets may carry upstream provider terms. Google Drive artifacts not inspected; no weights downloaded or run; unrefereed preprint, accuracy claims not reproduced. Same family was proposed in the protein and complex lanes; one record.

name: BioKinema
description: Spatial-temporal diffusion model from IDEA, built on a frozen Protenix encoder and trained on ~54.6 ms of MD, that generates continuous-time all-atom trajectories for proteins and protein-ligand complexes; reported in a preprint to recover ensemble thermodynamics and kinetics as a fast complement to molecular dynamics.
status: Apache-2.0 code; weights and processed training-data bundle under CC BY-NC 4.0 on Hugging Face, ungated; non-commercial terms apply to at least one artifact or access route
io: Initial protein or protein-ligand complex structure (PDB/mmCIF) + checkpoint-matched time-scaling exponent -> generated continuous-time all-atom trajectory; replica trajectories pooled for ensemble and kinetics (TICA/MSM) analysis
use_cases: MD-surrogate trajectory generation, conformational-ensemble and kinetics analysis, ligand-induced conformational change and allostery; ligand-unbinding pathways after fine-tuning on metadynamics data (fine-tuned checkpoint not released)
audit_note: Verified 2026-10-10: bioRxiv record (v1 2026-02-15, v2 2026-08-18), official IDEA-XL repository (Apache-2.0 code, CC BY-NC 4.0 DATA_LICENSE) and Hugging Face API (two ungated ~4.2 GB checkpoints plus ~44 GB processed-data bundle, card licence cc-by-nc-4.0). Weights sit on the first author's personal hub account, linked from the official repository. Each checkpoint needs its matching time-scaling exponent; the long-time checkpoint is single-chain only. Unbinding results used a metadynamics fine-tune that is not released. Unrefereed preprint; no model execution.

name: ODesign
description: All-atom generative model for epitope-conditioned design of protein, small-molecule and nucleic-acid binding partners against arbitrary biomolecular targets, whose code builds on Protenix and OpenFold.
status: Open code + weights (Apache-2.0), ungated on Hugging Face; web server reachable (access terms not inspected)
io: Target structure + epitope/hotspot specification + design modality -> designed all-atom binder complexes (protein, small-molecule ligand or nucleic acid) with sequences
use_cases: Epitope-targeted protein binder design, structure-based ligand design, protein-binding RNA/DNA design, cyclic-peptide binder design, atom and motif scaffolding, partial redesign of an existing binder, cross-modality interaction design
audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-10-10 from the arXiv API record (2510.22304v2), the official repository README, LICENSE, license_file_list.md and ckpt/get_odesign_ckpt.sh, and the Hugging Face API. Four ODesign base checkpoints (~4.3 GB each) plus four OInvFold inverse-folding checkpoints and a separate ODesign-AB checkpoint are public, ungated and tagged apache-2.0; no weights downloaded. The GitHub repo was renamed from The-Institute-for-AI-Molecular-Design/ODesign to OTeam-AI4S/ODesign (old path redirects); the Hugging Face org keeps the old name and is official because the repo's own downloader points at it. GitHub licence detection reports NOASSERTION because the Apache 2.0 text carries a custom header; the file grants commercial use. Not inspected: the Google Drive inference/training data folder (no licence seen, ~850 GB archive) and the web server's own terms (JS-only page), so neither is evidence of open access. Default training initialises from an external Protenix v0.5.0 checkpoint. Unrefereed preprint: Europe PMC search returned no journal version on 2026-10-10. Design model: the protein-design lane may also claim it; deduplicate across lanes (precedent: Proteina-Complexa is 'complex', BoltzGen and PXDesign are 'protein').

name: BOTANIC-1 (Botanic1-S / -M / -L)
description: Plant genomic language models from Living Models (the family after BOTANIC-0): bidirectional Mamba-2 encoders pretrained by masked language modelling on single-nucleotide tokens from 320 land-plant species, released at 318M, 688M and 2.1B parameters. The technical report also describes a 3.2B XL model, listed as private on the hub, and a context-extended 318M model reaching 128 kbp that is not among the released checkpoints. A sparse-autoencoder repository for Botanic1-M exposes interpretable sequence features.
status: Weights, model code and tutorials for S, M and L sit in auto-gated Hugging Face repositories (contact sharing plus a non-commercial-research checkbox) under the custom livingmodels-research licence: revocable, research use only, commercial use only under a separate licence, no distillation or training of similar models. The pre-training corpus and the sparse autoencoder use the same gate and licence. Botanic1-XL (3.2B) is private and the 128 kbp checkpoint is not released.
io: Plant DNA sequence as single-nucleotide tokens (released checkpoints pretrained on 8,192-token windows; longer inputs untested) -> per-nucleotide embeddings and masked-token predictions for zero-shot variant scoring, probing and fine-tuning
use_cases: Zero-shot variant-effect scoring and causal-variant prioritisation, probing of coding and regulatory features, fine-tuning for promoter and terminator strength, chromatin accessibility and transcription-factor binding in plants
audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-10-10 from the bioRxiv v3 full text (JATS XML), the hub API and visible cards of all three model repositories, the SAE and dataset cards, the official collection and the licence text shown on the public LICENSE blob page. No gate was accepted and no weights were downloaded. The report's availability section lists a Botanic1-XL repository, but it returns 401 and the cards mark XL as private; the 128 kbp context-extended checkpoint is not on the hub and its corpora are marked as planned. Benchmark claims are author-reported. Kept separate from BOTANIC-0 (new report, BiMamba2 single-nucleotide architecture, 320-species corpus); no deprecation of BOTANIC-0 is implied.

name: LOAM (LOAM-25M / 100M / 340M / 624M)
description: Decoder-only genomic language model family from Soilytix (25M-624M parameters) trained at single-nucleotide resolution exclusively on Oxford Nanopore long-read metagenome-assembled genomes from Microflora Danica, a Danish survey of soil, sediment and water microbiomes (67.5 Gbp corpus of 15,640 species-representative MAGs).
status: Weights CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 behind an auto-approved Hugging Face gate (shares username and e-mail; asks affiliation and a non-commercial-research agreement) plus a separate acceptable-use policy; model code and tokenizer stated as Apache-2.0; benchmark code Apache-2.0
io: Prokaryotic DNA sequence (uppercase A/C/G/T, up to 8,192 nt) -> next-nucleotide likelihoods, per-nucleotide embeddings and sampled DNA continuations
use_cases: Zero-shot variant-effect scoring, gene-essentiality and enzyme-function prediction from linear probes on frozen embeddings; DNA continuation sampling is offered on the model card but was not evaluated in the preprint
audit_note: Adversarial review 2026-10-10. Preprint (bioRxiv/openRxiv DOI 10.64898/2026.09.28.755120, posted 2026-10-02, CC BY-NC 4.0) names the Soilytix HF collection and gLMBench as the model and code availability routes. All four HF repos list model.safetensors with sizes consistent with fp32 parameter counts; gated=auto. Weights licence read in full (public LICENSE); LICENSE.code, USE_POLICY.md and NOTICE return 401 without accepting the gate, so the Apache-2.0 code term rests on the card and the LICENSE scope paragraph, and the acceptable-use terms are unread. The gate prompt limits use to non-commercial research, narrower than CC BY-NC-SA alone. Card citation still says the preprint is forthcoming. No pathogen screen was applied to the training corpus (card). Generation is a card workflow only, not benchmarked.

name: MicroGlot
description: Taxonomy-informed sparse mixture-of-experts DNA foundation model (2.98B total, 479M active parameters per token) pretrained on 378.3 billion nucleotides from 99,700 microbial species; hyperbolic taxonomy embeddings serve as an input token and steer expert routing. The release also includes MicroGlot-plain, a taxonomy-ablated variant, and a Species-encoder that infers species embeddings from DNA.
status: Open code (MIT on GitHub; hub copy CC BY 4.0) + weights (CC BY 4.0, ungated, Hugging Face); pretraining corpus not redistributed (public NCBI RefSeq).
io: Microbial DNA sequence (up to 8,192 BPE tokens, about 43 kb) plus an NCBI species name for MicroGlot (missing names inferred by the Species-encoder) or DNA alone for MicroGlot-plain -> layer-wise embeddings and next-token logits
use_cases: Microbial phenotypic-trait and taxonomy probing, fine-tuning for microbial genomics tasks, species-aware representation learning
audit_note: Discovery and adversarial review 2026-10-10. Preprint Code availability names the author-owned GitHub (MIT) and Hugging Face repo; hub lists MicroGlot, MicroGlot-plain and Species-encoder safetensors (about 6 GB each), ungated, CC BY 4.0. Loading requires trust_remote_code and, per the card, FlashAttention-2 on an NVIDIA GPU; generation not supported. Species table derived from NCBI/ICTV/PLSDB, whose own terms also apply. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

name: Cerberus
description: Calico sequence-to-function model that replaces Borzoi's transformer blocks with bidirectional Mamba-2 (Hydra) state-space blocks; an ensemble of eight 138M-parameter models reads 786 kb of DNA and predicts 8,361 human and 3,102 mouse functional-genomics tracks at 32 bp resolution.
status: Apache-2.0 code; eight ungated weight files on a public Google Cloud bucket, with no licence stated for the weights; processed training data not yet released
io: 786 kb DNA window -> RNA-seq, CAGE, DNase/ATAC, ChIP, 3' RNA-seq (human and mouse heads) and CLIP (human only) coverage at 32 bp resolution; derived variant scores
use_cases: eQTL/sQTL/paQTL variant-effect scoring, regulatory-activity prediction, in silico mutagenesis and attribution, transfer learning to new assays
audit_note: Discovery and adversarial review 2026-10-10. Preprint v1, not peer reviewed. Code Apache-2.0; the weights carry no licence statement and none is present in the bucket. All eight model_best.pth files were confirmed by public bucket listing and HTTP HEAD, not downloaded. Requires an NVIDIA GPU (mamba-ssm Triton kernel). The preprint abstract says the training data is released, but releases/cerberus/README.md says processed training data release is pending. Distinct from Borzoi (bfm-borzoi), which the same repo now also serves in PyTorch.

name: RAGenome
description: Retrieval-based genomic language model (168M parameters) that retrieves homologous sequences from a 100-vertebrate whole-genome alignment at pretraining and inference time, combining intra-species local attention with inter-species cross-attention to extend alignment-based gLMs to 13,312-nucleotide contexts.
status: Open code + weights (MIT), ungated; inference needs the 100-way whole-genome alignment (public MIT-tagged Hugging Face dataset) and the taxonomy metadata shipped in the repository; human (hg38) query only
io: Human (hg38) DNA query (up to 13,312 nt) plus retrieved aligned sequences from other vertebrates -> nucleotide likelihoods and embeddings; variant scores as reference/alternate log-likelihood ratios
use_cases: Gene finding from frozen embeddings (BEND), zero-shot pathogenic-variant prioritization (ClinVar), evolution-aware representations of human genomic sequence
audit_note: Discovery 2026-10-10; adversarial re-check 2026-10-10. arXiv v1 posted 2026-10-08 (ML4Molecules workshop, NeurIPS 2026); abstract links the GitHub repo, whose README points to the pantoniadis/RAGenome checkpoint (account of co-author Panagiotis Antoniadis). GitHub LICENSE MIT; HF card MIT, ungated, model.safetensors listed (~672 MB, consistent with 168M fp32). Required alignment dataset songlab/multiz100way-pigz is ungated and MIT-tagged. Trained with Homo sapiens as query species; the paper says other species would likely need further pretraining. Evaluated on two tasks only (BEND gene finding MCC 0.60; ClinVar AUROC 0.87, below GPN-MSA/GPN-Star). Earlier dnafm/168M_rag_* checkpoints are not referenced by the official repo and are not the release.

name: RegFM
description: Context-aware foundation model for human transcriptional regulation. It couples a 650 kbp gene-centred cis-DNA transformer (LongNet dilated attention) with a trans-regulator module that encodes the expression of 2,103 transcription factors and chromatin regulators, joined by cross-attention. Pretraining runs in stages: masked language modelling on the GRCh38 genome and on TF/CR expression, then expression prediction on ENCODE and CELLxGENE transcriptomes. The aim is to predict gene expression in unseen cellular contexts.
status: Open code + weights (MIT), ungated; bundled customised transformers files keep their Apache-2.0 headers. Training data are third-party public (ENCODE, CELLxGENE) and not redistributed; no input-preprocessing code released
io: Gene-centred DNA sequence (650 kbp around the TSS) plus a 2,103-dimensional TF/CR expression profile for a cell context -> gene expression prediction and regulatory representations
use_cases: Gene expression prediction in unseen cell contexts (released scripts and demos); per the paper, fine-tuning for cis-regulatory element annotation, bivalent-promoter and dosage-sensitivity classification, and perturbation-response prediction, plus in silico TF knockout (pipelines not released)
audit_note: Discovery and adversarial review both on 2026-10-10. MIT code and weights verified on GitHub and the Hub; ungated. The Hub has three undocumented checkpoint folders (AllProtein, HVG, PBMC), distinct by hash, all expression-prediction-stage ('genepred') models. AllProtein likely corresponds to the paper's full ENCODE all-protein-coding model, and PBMC to the leave-one-out demo (inferred from names). MLM-stage module checkpoints are not released. Released code covers gene-expression training and prediction only. Users must build tokenized DNA and TF/CR input features themselves. The preprint text is CC BY-NC-ND; that does not apply to the model artifacts. No checkpoint was downloaded or loaded. The card says the DOI will be added later.

name: TomatoPGFM
description: Graph-conditioned genomic foundation model for tomato (479M parameters; bidirectional Mamba2 and local-attention mixture-of-experts blocks with a token-aligned graph adapter), pretrained by masked language modelling and graph-feature reconstruction on 54.65 Gb from 66 tomato accessions using pangenome node features and adjacency.
status: Open code + ungated inference weights (Hugging Face, ModelScope, Zenodo); Apache-2.0 declared for both, but the shipped LICENSE is an abridged Apache-2.0 text; processed evaluation data CC BY 4.0; training-resume checkpoint not released
io: Tomato DNA sequence (reverse-complement-folded 6-mer tokens), optionally with token-aligned pangenome-graph node features and adjacency -> masked-token predictions and sequence embeddings; LoRA-adapted task predictions
use_cases: Tomato sequence embeddings and LoRA fine-tuning (reported: gene- and CDS-versus-intergenic classification in two held-out accessions); graph-conditioned masked-token modelling of pangenome sequence
audit_note: Adversarial review 2026-10-10. GitHub, Hugging Face, ModelScope and Zenodo are all listed in the preprint; the same model.safetensors (1,916,843,008 bytes, matching SHA-256) is on HF, ModelScope and Zenodo. Apache-2.0 is declared in README, MODEL_WEIGHTS.md, CITATION.cff and hub/Zenodo metadata; the shipped LICENSE omits several standard Apache-2.0 clauses (GitHub: NOASSERTION). Single-genus model; downstream tests are gene- and CDS-vs-intergenic classification on two held-out accessions (frozen probes and LoRA) with graph input disabled; PlantDNAMamba scored higher and DNABERT-2 lower in all four comparisons. Inference needs CUDA mamba-ssm; not Transformers-native. Nothing downloaded or executed.

name: Evo2HiC
description: Genome sequence-and-structure foundation model that distils Evo 2 (7B) into a compact 3.6M-parameter CNN sequence encoder under Hi-C guidance, with a DNA-only encoder and a sequence-plus-Hi-C encoder for cell-type-specific 3D genome analysis.
status: Open code + pretrained weights and task-specific weights for Hi-C resolution enhancement and epigenomic prediction (Apache-2.0), ungated Zenodo archive
io: DNA sequence, optionally with Hi-C contact maps -> Hi-C contact-matrix predictions, enhanced-resolution Hi-C, epigenomic profiles and joint embeddings
use_cases: Hi-C contact prediction from sequence (after fine-tuning the pretrained checkpoint), Hi-C resolution enhancement including cross-species maps, epigenomic assay prediction, cell-type-specific motif discovery by attribution of Hi-C-conditioned epigenomic predictions
audit_note: Discovery 2026-10-10 (older model absent from the catalog); adversarially reviewed 2026-10-10. The paper's Code Availability (v1 and v2) links the GitHub repo with weights under Apache 2.0. Zenodo record (creator: first author; isSupplementTo the preprint DOI) is Apache-2.0, open, one 1.47 GB tar.zst. Its description lists pretraining, resolution-enhancement and epigenomic-prediction models. The archive contents were not opened. The preprint text is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (paper only, not code or weights). Distilled from Evo 2; separate from HiCFoundation (bfm-hicfoundation).

name: Minerva (Minerva-MLM)
description: 650M-parameter mixed-modality genome language model (amino-acid tokens for genes, nucleotide tokens for intergenic regions) initialised from gLM2 650M and continued-pretrained for about a trillion tokens on OMG metagenomes and GlobDB genomes, with an 8,192-token variant (Minerva-MLM-8k); checkpoints ship interaction heads for alignment-free prediction of RNA base pairing, protein contacts and repeats.
status: Open code + weights (Apache-2.0), ungated Hugging Face checkpoints (custom model code); no new training data released (trained on public OMG and GlobDB corpora)
io: Prokaryotic genomic sequence as mixed tokens (amino-acid tokens for coding regions, nucleotide tokens for intergenic regions; up to 4,096 or 8,192 tokens; raw DNA via Pyrodigal gene calling) -> masked-token predictions, embeddings and two-dimensional interaction maps (base pairing, protein contacts, repeats)
use_cases: Non-coding RNA discovery and base-pairing prediction, protein contact prediction, repeat detection, genome annotation by coevolutionary mining; family-specific finetuning
audit_note: Discovery 2026-10-10; adversarial review 2026-10-10. Apache-2.0 code (GitHub) and weights (both HF repos: cardData and LICENSE file, ungated, model.safetensors listed) verified; parent gLM2_650M also Apache-2.0. Preprint v2 full text read from bioRxiv JATS XML: initialised from gLM2 650M, continued pretraining on OMG (25%) + GlobDB r226 (75%), 1.2M steps at 4,096 tokens, then 620k steps at 8,192 tokens for Minerva-MLM-8k. The repository README states 'over 1.3 trillion tokens' in total, while the preprint says continued pretraining was 'a trillion tokens'; the record uses the preprint figure. Training corpora are third-party and their terms were not checked. Family relation: derived from gLM2 (proposed separately). The README also mentions a RiNALMo-based eukaryotic RNA checkpoint, which was not reviewed and is not part of this record.

name: NTv3 (Nucleotide Transformer v3)
description: InstaDeep multi-species genomic foundation model with a U-Net-like architecture and single-base tokenization, pretrained on 9 trillion bp from OpenGenome2 with contexts up to 1 Mb and post-trained on about 16,000 functional tracks and annotations from 24 animal and plant species. Released as 8M, 100M and 650M pre-trained and 100M and 650M post-trained checkpoints; a fine-tuned generative (masked-diffusion) variant supports enhancer design.
status: JAX code on GitHub under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; PyTorch model code and weights on Hugging Face behind an automatic gate under a custom InstaDeep non-commercial model licence (full text readable only after accepting the gate)
io: DNA sequence (up to 1 Mb, length a multiple of 128), plus a species token for post-trained models -> masked-token predictions, embeddings, functional-track (BigWig) and genome-annotation (BED) predictions
use_cases: Cross-species functional-track prediction, genome annotation, fine-tuning for regulatory and annotation tasks, variant-effect interpretation, controllable enhancer design
audit_note: Discovery 2026-10-10 (older model absent from the catalog); adversarial review 2026-10-10. Paper, GitHub and HF org cross-link one another. GitHub LICENSE.md (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) covers the JAX code; HF weights and the PyTorch code repo (InstaDeepAI/ntv3_base_model) are auto-gated, licence 'other'; MODEL-LICENSE.md returns 401, so terms come from the card's licence summary (non-commercial only; output and derivative-model restrictions). NTv3 benchmark dataset auto-gated, CC BY-NC 4.0. Pre/post cards carry a paper placeholder; the generative card links the bioRxiv paper. Separate from bfm-nucleotide-transformer (v1/v2).

name: gLM2
description: Tatta Bio mixed-modality genomic language model (masked-LM transformer encoder) that reads protein-coding sequences as amino-acid tokens and intergenic regions as nucleotide tokens, trained on the semantically deduplicated Open MetaGenomic (OMG) corpus at 150M and 650M parameters.
status: Open code + weights (Apache-2.0: GitHub LICENSE; Hugging Face card metadata), ungated checkpoints at 150M and 650M (custom model code); OMG training corpus public under CC BY-SA 4.0
io: Genomic contig of up to 4,096 tokens as strand-tagged amino-acid CDS tokens and nucleotide intergenic tokens -> contextual embeddings and masked-token predictions; categorical-Jacobian maps for co-evolution analysis
use_cases: Genomic-context protein and DNA embeddings (DGEB tasks), protein-protein interface contacts from co-evolutionary signal, intergenic regulatory-syntax analysis, metagenomic representation learning and transfer
audit_note: Catalog-gap addition (2024 model, not a release in the October window); adversarial review 2026-10-10. Preprint v1 2024-08-17 and v2 2024-10-01; bioRxiv lists no journal version, and a peer-reviewed venue is UNVERIFIED. v2 matches the hosted checkpoints (4,096-token context, per-nucleotide intergenic tokens); v1 described the superseded 2,048-token/BPE configuration. Both Hugging Face repos are ungated with cardData apache-2.0 and model.safetensors listed (weights last changed Sep 2024); GitHub LICENSE Apache-2.0; OMG dataset card CC BY-SA 4.0. Distinct from gLM (bfm-glm-genomic-language-model). Derivative Tatta checkpoints are not covered: gLM2_650M_bgc_decoder CC BY-NC 4.0; gLM2_650M_UR50, gLM2_150M_no_prune and gLM2_650M_sae carry no licence metadata. Upstream IMG/MGnify data terms not reviewed. Nothing downloaded or executed.

name: EpiZoo
description: DNA sequence-aware single-cell epigenomics foundation model (mixture-of-experts transformer, about 2.6 billion parameters) pretrained on Omni-scATAC, a curated corpus of about 20.9 million human and mouse scATAC-seq cells. Accessible cCREs become cell-sentence tokens that combine a DNA-sequence embedding, an identity embedding and an accessibility-rank embedding; the model can be post-trained for further species.
status: Open MIT code; one pretrained base checkpoint distributed through a public Google Drive link in the official README, with no separate weight licence (README states the project is MIT); pretraining data are public source datasets listed in the preprint supplement
io: scATAC-seq profiles tokenized as TF-IDF-ranked accessible cCREs with their DNA sequences -> cell embeddings; after fine-tuning or extension training: cell-type labels, imputed accessibility and cell-type-specific accessibility predicted from DNA sequence
use_cases: scATAC cell embedding and clustering, cell-type annotation, accessibility imputation, post-training for new species, human-macaque regulatory comparison, noncoding somatic mutation prioritization (EpiZoo-Cancer extension)
audit_note: Discovery (DNA and single-cell lanes, merged) and adversarial review 2026-10-10. Preprint v1, not peer reviewed; full text read from bioRxiv JATS XML. Code MIT. Single base checkpoint pretrained_EpiZoo.pth on a public Google Drive link from the README; view page seen, file not downloaded; no separate weight licence. Fine-tuned, EpiZoo-Evo, EpiZoo-Cancer and sequence-prediction variants are trained by the user with repo code; no released checkpoints found. SEAM config files derive from DNABERT-2 (Apache-2.0 file in repo). Preprint text is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (paper only). Same group as EpiAgent (bfm-epiagent), whose pretraining data Omni-scATAC includes; separate model.

name: EukaUTR
description: 3' UTR-specific RNA language model (ESM-2-style encoder, about 87M parameters) pretrained by masked-language modelling at single-nucleotide resolution in two species-disjoint stages on about 7.08 million non-redundant eukaryotic 3' UTRs from 1,719 genomes. The released checkpoints provide embeddings for fine-tuning on post-transcriptional prediction tasks and support de novo 3' UTR generation and stability-guided editing, evaluated in silico.
status: Open code (MIT) + ungated Hugging Face checkpoints declared MIT in the hub card metadata; pretraining and benchmark data CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo. No fine-tuned task heads released.
io: 3' UTR DNA/RNA sequence (up to 1,022 nt per input window) -> embeddings and masked-token predictions; user fine-tuning -> stability, expression and RNA-fate predictions; iterative masked decoding -> generated or edited 3' UTRs
use_cases: 3' UTR representation learning, mRNA stability and expression prediction after fine-tuning, de novo 3' UTR design and in silico guided sequence optimisation
audit_note: Verified from primary sources on 2026-10-10 (adversarial re-check). Paper code-availability statement names the GitHub repo (MIT) and the Hugging Face checkpoint repo; Zenodo creators match the paper authors. Hub file listing, sizes and licence metadata were inspected; nothing was downloaded or executed. The weights' MIT grant rests only on the hub card metadata (no LICENSE file there). The README's per-file checkpoint links point to subfolders and return 404 (files sit at the hub repo root), and the packaged EukaUTR-Guide direction file is not published; custom directions can be built from steering sets in the repository. The repository has no pretraining or fine-tuning scripts and no fine-tuned task heads. Guided editing is evaluated in silico only; task performance figures are author-reported.

name: CodonMamba
description: 71M-parameter bidirectional Mamba codon language model pretrained by masked codon prediction on about 9 million coding sequences from 1,544 organisms (the CaLM corpus). The released checkpoint provides codon-level embeddings for training mRNA property predictors and generates protein-preserving synonymous coding sequences that can be steered at inference time by a host codon-usage table.
status: Open code (MIT; bundled Mamba kernels Apache-2.0) + weights (single ungated HF checkpoint, MIT declared in card metadata); pretraining corpus not redistributed
io: Coding sequence as codon tokens (up to 1,024 codons) -> codon-level embeddings for user-trained property heads; protein sequence plus optional host codon-usage table -> synonymous CDS by iterative masked infilling
use_cases: mRNA property prediction from frozen embeddings (protein expression, mRNA stability and degradation, regulatory phenotypes), codon optimization and cross-host retargeting, coding-sequence representation learning
audit_note: Verified from primary sources on 2026-10-10. The preprint's code and data availability statement names both the Hugging Face checkpoint and the GitHub repository. Only the pretrained backbone is released (no fine-tuned task heads); the hub card is metadata only. The checkpoint (837 MB pickle, loaded with weights_only=False) was listed, not downloaded or executed. Benchmark rankings are author-reported.

name: OmicsFM
description: Transformer pretrained by masked abundance reconstruction on 48,837 quality-filtered proteomics profiles (1,397 PRIDE projects reprocessed, 1,143 contributing profiles). The same architecture was trained separately on ARCHS4 bulk RNA-seq and CELLxGENE Census single-cell data. Sample and protein/gene embeddings transferred to cell-type, gene-essentiality and perturbation-response prediction.
status: Apache-2.0 code on GitHub and in the current PyPI wheel (the PyPI page still shows MIT from an earlier 1.0.0 build); public, ungated checkpoints labelled CC BY 4.0 on Hugging Face; transcriptomic training corpora public under CC BY 4.0; proteomics training corpus not yet released.
io: Proteomics or transcriptomics abundance profile (binned, up to 1,024 features per pass) -> sample summary embedding, protein/gene identity embeddings, attention-derived protein/gene association rankings
use_cases: Proteomics sample representation, zero-shot protein-association networks from attention, cross-omics comparison, cell-type classification, gene-essentiality and perturbation-response prediction
audit_note: Verified from primary sources on 2026-10-10 (bioRxiv and Crossref, GitHub API, Hugging Face API, PyPI JSON and per-file metadata, Zenodo API). Modality routing is a curator decision: the hub holds separately trained single-modality checkpoints (proteomics, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics), not a jointly trained multimodal model. The hub lists seven checkpoint folders, the six in the paper plus an Ensembl-vocabulary single-cell ablation. The README and hub.py still say checkpoints are private until publication; the hub API reports them public and ungated. ESM-C variants ship precomputed ESM-C 600M embeddings; the upstream ESM-C 600M hub card currently lists MIT. Preprint not peer reviewed. Nothing was downloaded or executed.

name: ShEPhERD-2
description: 3D molecular generative diffusion model conditioned on an explicit interaction profile of shape, electrostatics and directional pharmacophores. Trained on MOSES drug-like molecules; a single model checkpoint (MOSES-aq) supports pharmacophore prioritization, substructure constraints and composition of profiles, and is applied to fragment merging, dual-target design, selectivity engineering and modality hopping without task-specific retraining.
status: Open code + weights (MIT); ungated MOSES-aq hub checkpoints fetched automatically by the package, with MIT-labelled supplementary data including training HDF5 on Zenodo. Inference needs GFN2-xTB installed separately.
io: Interaction profile extracted from a reference 3D structure or from SMILES -> generated 3D molecular structures, xTB-relaxed by default
use_cases: Interaction-conditioned molecular generation, bioisosteric fragment merging, dual-target and selectivity design, ligand-interaction-conditioned design without pocket-geometry conditioning
audit_note: Independently re-verified from primary sources on 2026-10-10. Code MIT (repository LICENSE, 'Coley Research Group @ MIT'); hub repo kabeywar/shepherd2 ungated with card metadata license: mit and no separate weights LICENSE file; Zenodo deposit metadata licence mit-license. Ownership resolved: the hub account is Kento Abeywardane, a member of the Coley Research Group organization on the hub, the official repository hardcodes that repo id for automatic checkpoint download, and the preprint links the hub page. File listing and metadata were inspected and a HEAD request confirmed the checkpoint; nothing was downloaded or executed. Only the MOSES-aq model line is released (inference 25.6 MB, resume 76.5 MB), so the released chemical space is neutral drug-like molecules; inference requires an external GFN2-xTB installation. The pinned Zenodo version DOI matches the preprint's citation; the repository README cites concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22675705, which now resolves to a newer version (10.5281/zenodo.22798054, 2026-09-16, same MIT licence).

name: InstaNovo-FM
description: Self-supervised encoder-only transformer (~89.5M parameters) for bottom-up proteomics, pretrained by physics-aware masked reconstruction of tandem mass spectra without peptide-sequence labels. The released models were trained on the 184.6-million-PSM annotated tier of a 1.63-billion-spectrum corpus from 92 PRIDE submissions. Their frozen spectrum embeddings support de novo sequencing, database-free identification, PTM detection and run classification.
status: Apache-2.0 code; five pretrained encoder checkpoints and three de novo sequencer checkpoints on the v0.1.0 GitHub release under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike), ungated; the derived embeddings dataset is also CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; released corpus tiers follow EMBL-EBI terms of use, and the unlabelled 1.63B-spectrum tier is not redistributed.
io: Tandem mass spectrum (MS/MS) -> 768-d spectrum embedding; downstream: peptide sequence via attached decoder, peptide identity via embedding nearest-neighbour retrieval, run-level condition labels via aggregated embeddings
use_cases: Proteomics spectrum representation learning, de novo peptide sequencing, database-free identification and spectrum rescue, PTM and glycan detection, run-level classification of acquisition and experimental conditions
audit_note: Adversarially re-verified from primary sources on 2026-10-10. Paper Code availability names the InstaDeep repository and its Releases; repository and release notes cite the same DOI. The released models were trained on the LCFM annotated tier (184.6M PSMs), not on the full 1.63B-spectrum corpus, which is not redistributed. Modality routing is a curation choice: the model reads mass spectra rather than protein sequences, and the catalog has no spectra modality. Asset names and per-artifact licences were read from the repository README, release notes and model registry; no checkpoint was downloaded or executed. One of the eight checkpoints is a from-scratch control without pretraining. Non-commercial share-alike terms cover the weights and the embeddings dataset.

name: Prot-LAMBDA / LambdaFold
description: Protein language model initialized from ESM2-650M, with its top 11 of 33 layers further trained on PDB and AlphaFold DB structures using masked language modelling plus explicit inter-residue contact supervision. Released together with LambdaFold, a lightweight distance-guided single-sequence structure predictor, and LambdaFold-RAG, a template-fusion refinement module.
status: Open code + ungated weights (GPL-3.0 on GitHub and in the Hugging Face card metadata). The preprint describes code and weights as freely available for academic use, and the README offers a different licence, for example for commercial use, on request. A CC BY 4.0 Zenodo record holds predictions, not parameters.
io: Protein sequence -> per-residue and pair embeddings, masked-token logits and contact maps; sequence -> multi-stage distograms, 3D structure (PDB) with pLDDT; sequence plus a user-supplied precomputed structural template -> refined 3D structure
use_cases: Structure-aware protein embeddings for downstream probes (evaluated in the preprint on secondary structure, dihedral angles, solvent accessibility, disorder and fold), contact and distogram prediction, single-sequence structure prediction, template-guided structure refinement
audit_note: Verified from primary sources on 2026-10-10 (adversarial review). The preprint's Code Availability names the GitHub repository and the KiharaLab Hugging Face repository; the hub listing shows ProtLAMBDA.pth, DistFormer.pth, LambdaFold.pth and RAG.pth, the filenames the example notebooks load (inspected, not downloaded or run). The GitHub README points to Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.21984993 for parameters, but that record holds predicted contact maps, distograms and structures only. The hub card's LICENSE link returns 404, so hub terms rest on the gpl-3.0 metadata and card text. The preprint's 'freely available for academic use' wording does not change the GPL-3.0 grant; noncommercial=false follows the licence files. Upstream code: ESM (MIT), OpenFold (Apache-2.0). The RAG demo uses a precomputed template file; template search is not included. Unrelated to the LAMBDA prophage benchmark (bfm-lambda).

name: CytoBERT
description: Self-supervised Transformer foundation model for single-cell cytometry with variable marker panels: each cell is tokenized as marker-expression pairs over a shared 220-marker vocabulary, so studies with different antibody panels share one encoder. Pretrained by masked expression-bin prediction on about 50 million cells from 15 human CyTOF datasets from ImmPort.
status: Open, not gated: MIT code (GitHub and Zenodo code snapshot); pretrained checkpoint and preprocessed ImmPort-derived data in a CC BY 4.0 Zenodo archive; CC BY 4.0 Docker image on Zenodo; no API or server.
io: Single-cell cytometry marker-expression pairs (variable panels) -> cell-level CLS embeddings; pooled cell sets with fine-tuned heads -> sample-level classification
use_cases: Transfer learning across CyTOF studies with heterogeneous panels; sample-level disease/condition classification (e.g. transplant, autoimmunity, HIV, COVID-19 severity, liver cancer stage, peanut allergy; evaluated in the paper); cell-type classification and reference mapping from embeddings (repository tutorials only)
audit_note: Verified from primary sources on 2026-10-10. arXiv preprint (cs.LG, v1 14 Aug 2026); arXiv lists no venue, and the GitHub release v1.0 is titled 'REHMED@ECML'. Small model (d=128, 6 layers, 8 heads). The pretrained checkpoint (save/pretrain_run_dir/checkpoints__uniform/cytobert_epoch_50.pt, 4.9 MB) was seen in the Zenodo zip preview of the 9.2 GB archive, not downloaded. The paper evaluates only sample-level classification on 7 CyTOF datasets; CytoBERT had the best average rank under grouped splits, but differences between models were not significant (Friedman p=0.093). The repository's cell-classification tutorial uses a separate cell_tasks checkpoint (epoch 100) also shipped in the zip, which the paper does not describe. The MIT LICENSE names 'Anonymous' as copyright holder. Re-pretraining from scratch requires downloading the source datasets from ImmPort under the ImmPort user agreement (no non-commercial clause; redistribution on commensurate terms).

name: GENERanno
description: Genomic foundation model family from GenerTeam (developers of GENERator) built for gene annotation. Its 0.5B-parameter bidirectional transformer encoders use single-nucleotide tokens and an 8 kb context and were pretrained by masked language modelling: the prokaryotic model on 715 Gbp (described in the preprint) and a eukaryotic model on 386 Gbp (documented only in the hub card as in development). Fine-tuned token-classification checkpoints call coding sequences (CDS): a 0.5B prokaryotic/metagenomic annotator and a 1.2B eukaryotic annotator released as a preview.
status: Open code + weights (MIT); base and annotator checkpoints public and ungated; benchmark and annotation datasets MIT.
io: DNA sequence (single-nucleotide tokens, up to 8 kb) -> contextual embeddings and masked-nucleotide predictions; CDS-annotator heads -> per-nucleotide coding-region labels
use_cases: Prokaryotic and metagenomic CDS annotation from fragmented sequence; eukaryotic CDS annotation (preview checkpoint); pseudogene prediction and taxonomic classification from raw sequence; embeddings and fine-tuning for prokaryotic sequence tasks such as gene fitness, antibiotic-resistance and gene classification
audit_note: Catalog-gap addition verified 2026-10-10 by an adversarial re-check; this is not a new release in the October window. The preprint (latest v3, 2025-08-14) describes only the prokaryotic model and lists a eukaryotic version as planned. The eukaryotic base (386 Gbp) and the 1.2B eukaryotic CDS annotator preview are documented only in the README and hub cards, which say technical details are still to come. File listings, gating and licence metadata were inspected for all four hub repos (all MIT, all ungated, all holding model.safetensors) and for three GenerTeam datasets (MIT). GitHub has no tagged releases, and its README table links for the two base models are malformed; the record links the correct repos. GENERanno is a separate encoder model from the displayed GENERator decoder by the same team. Nothing was downloaded or executed.

name: Profluent-E1
description: Family of retrieval-augmented masked protein language models (150M, 300M and 600M parameters) that can condition on unaligned homologous sequences prepended to the query; runs in single-sequence or retrieval-augmented mode.
status: Inference code Apache-2.0 when used apart from the weights; weights and full release under the custom Profluent-E1 Clickthrough License: commercial use allowed, with notice and attribution duties (drugs and targets found with it must be labelled 'Built with Profluent-E1'), terms Profluent may amend, and termination on breach. Three ungated Hugging Face checkpoints; no training code or data.
io: Protein sequence, optionally preceded by user-supplied homologs or context sampled from an A3M MSA -> per-residue embeddings and masked-token logits
use_cases: Protein embeddings, zero-shot fitness and variant-effect scoring, unsupervised contact-map prediction
audit_note: Catalog-gap addition checked on 2026-10-10; E1 was released in November 2025, so it is not new in the October window. LICENSE, NOTICE and ATTRIBUTION were read in full: no non-commercial clause, but a bespoke agreement accepted by download or use, with drug/target labelling, arbitration, amendment and termination clauses. File listings of all three Hugging Face repositories were inspected (ungated, model.safetensors present); nothing was downloaded or executed. The preprint text is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; that licence covers the manuscript only.

name: GearNet
description: Geometry-aware relational graph neural network pretrained on AlphaFold DB protein structures with multiview-contrast and self-prediction objectives, giving structure-based protein representations for downstream function and property prediction; released checkpoints are the GearNet-Edge variant.
status: MIT code; five pretrained GearNet-Edge checkpoints on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0, open and ungated. Running the code requires the separate TorchDrug (TorchProtein) stack, Apache-2.0.
io: Protein 3D structure graph -> residue and protein embeddings; task heads -> function and property predictions
use_cases: Structure-based protein representation learning; fine-tuning for EC, GO, fold and reaction classification; comparing structure-pretraining objectives
audit_note: Catalog-gap addition verified on 2026-10-10; not a new release in the October window. The Zenodo file listing and licence were inspected (v1 record 7593637, linked from the README; a v2 record 7723075 adds a fold_mc_gearnet_edge_ieconv.pth file). Repository (MIT) and TorchDrug (Apache-2.0) licences were confirmed via the GitHub API. Nothing was downloaded or executed. The README installation pins PyTorch 1.8.0, and TorchDrug was last pushed 2024-08-12. The ICLR 2023 venue was confirmed via the OpenReview API; the arXiv entry is the accessible primary source.

name: HIPT
description: Hierarchical vision transformer for gigapixel whole-slide pathology images, pretrained in two nested DINO self-supervised stages on pan-cancer TCGA H&E diagnostic slides (the paper reports 33 cancer types and about 10,700 slides). The released ViT-S/16 patch encoder (256 px) and ViT-XS region encoder (4,096 px) give reusable patch and region embeddings; slide-level representations come from averaging region embeddings or from training the lightweight slide-level transformer on labelled data.
status: Open code + weights (both checkpoints in the GitHub repository via Git LFS, ungated); non-commercial terms apply: LICENSE is Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause (no right to sell, including paid hosting or support), and the README states the code is available for non-commercial academic purposes. No separate terms for the weights.
io: H&E whole-slide image split into 256 x 256 patches and 4,096 x 4,096 regions -> 384-d patch embeddings and 192-d region embeddings; slide-level representation by mean-pooling region embeddings or a task-trained slide head
use_cases: Patch- and region-level feature extraction for whole-slide MIL, cancer subtyping, survival prediction, hierarchical attention visualization
audit_note: Catalog-gap addition verified 2026-10-10; not a new release in the October window. noncommercial=true rests on two statements: the LICENSE (Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause, which withholds the right to sell) and the README notice that the code is available for non-commercial academic purposes. Neither names the checkpoints separately; they sit in the same repository. Checkpoint availability was established from the LFS pointer files and Git LFS batch-API download actions for both objects (704,238,867 and 395,710,078 bytes), not by downloading or loading the weights. Pretraining stops at the 4K-region level; the slide-level transformer is trained per task. Repository last pushed 2024-03-19; no GitHub releases. An author-account Hugging Face repo (Richarizardd/HIPT) is an empty stub tagged GPL-3.0 with no weights and is not cited.

name: AIDO.Tissue (GB.Tissue)
description: Spatial transcriptomics foundation model in the GenBio AIDO family (3M and 60M parameters), pretrained on about 22 million cells from 76 spatial slides by encoding each centre cell together with its nearest spatial neighbours in an asymmetric encoder-decoder.
status: Code (ModelGenerator), ungated hub weights (3M, 60M) and downstream task data, all under the GenBio AI Community License: non-commercial use only for materials, derivatives and outputs, and outputs may not train competing models. Hub card metadata carry no licence field; the README badge links this licence.
io: Spatial single-cell expression of a centre cell plus its K nearest neighbour cells -> gene-level embeddings, pooled into cell embeddings; fine-tuned heads -> cell-type, niche-type and cell-density predictions
use_cases: Spatially contextualised cell embeddings, spatial cell-type and niche-type classification, cell-density estimation
audit_note: Catalog-gap addition verified 2026-10-10; not a new release in the October window. Identity chain: the preprint points to ModelGenerator for code and weights; ModelGenerator backbones gb_tissue_3m/gb_tissue_60m load genbio-ai/GB.Tissue-3M/-60M; the old AIDO.Tissue-* hub names redirect (307) to GB.Tissue-*. The hub cards do not cite the preprint, the backbone docstrings cite the AIDO.Cell manuscript instead, and card metrics (K=8) differ from the paper's best configurations, so which paper configuration each checkpoint matches is not stated. Terms: the GenBio AI Community License defines its scope as datasets, code and weights on the genbio-ai GitHub and Hugging Face pages; GitHub reports the licence as NOASSERTION. Nothing was downloaded or executed.

name: Riptides benchmark
description: Curated benchmark of 88 PDB-derived protein-peptide complexes (linear peptides and macrocycles; 51 non-canonical cyclic), released with evaluation code that reports full-atom and backbone RMSD plus PoseBusters validity for predicted peptide poses.
status: Open benchmark: evaluation code MIT; benchmark structures and Vilya-2 reference predictions CC BY 4.0, in one official GitHub repository; no tagged release or archive DOI. The Vilya-2 model itself is not released.
io: Predicted peptide (SDF) and receptor (PDB) structures per entry -> full-atom and backbone RMSD plus PoseBusters checks (results.csv)
use_cases: Evaluation of protein-peptide and macrocycle interface structure prediction; comparison of co-folding models with physics-based docking
audit_note: Verified 2026-10-10 as the one public artifact from the Vilya watchlist item; Vilya-1/Vilya-2 have no released weights or access route. Benchmark, not a foundation model. Paper (arXiv v1, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 text), repo README, MIT LICENSE, assets/LICENSE (CC BY 4.0) and the recursive file tree (88 ligand SDF + 88 receptor PDB; 88 Vilya-2 prediction pairs + results.csv) were inspected; the benchmark was not run and structures were not downloaded. Composition figures come from the authors' paper. Company-authored, not peer reviewed, no versioned release; time split (PDB entries after 2023-06-01) may overlap the training data of newer models.

name: scRep
description: Single-cell RNA-seq foundation model pretrained by teacher-student self-distillation in latent space at the cell and gene-token levels, with no expression-reconstruction objective; released as scRep-3M (about 2.8 million Tabula Sapiens and CELLxGENE cells) and scRep-30M (30.72 million CELLxGENE cells).
status: Open weights + model/inference code (Apache-2.0); ungated Hugging Face bundle with two checkpoints, not yet linked from the preprint; training/evaluation scripts and processed data promised on publication
io: scRNA-seq AnnData (.h5ad; Ensembl gene IDs matching the bundled vocabulary) -> 768-dimensional L2-normalised cell embeddings
use_cases: Frozen cell embeddings for clustering and cell-type annotation by label transfer; marker-gene prioritisation; TF-associated gene programs; developmental trajectory and pseudotime analysis
audit_note: Surfaced via the bio.rodeo feed (lead only). Verified 2026-10-10 against the bioRxiv v1 full text, Crossref, and the Hugging Face card, file listing, LICENSE (verbatim Apache-2.0), configs and checkpoint manifests. Provenance limit: the preprint does not link the hub repository and says checkpoints will be released on publication, and the card does not cite the paper. Attribution to the authors is based on the uploader display name matching the first and corresponding author (Shengjie Wang, Jilin University), the jlu-wsj handle, configs identical to the paper's architecture, and a 3M manifest totalling exactly the paper's 2,803,535 cells. Not established: whether the files are the exact checkpoints analysed in the paper. Benchmarks are author-reported; no weights were downloaded or run. Not to be confused with SCREP (single-cell drug-response prediction, 2024) or screp (scRNA-seq enrichment-plot R package).

name: InsilicoCell
description: Supervised multi-modal, multi-task transformer pretrained on more than 88 million labelled measurements across seven tasks. It links cell-line transcriptomes with compounds, genes and proteins to predict drug sensitivity, drug-induced expression, drug-protein binding, TF-gene association, gene dependency, mutation status and copy number, and supports multi-objective virtual drug screening.
status: Apache-2.0 inference code (architecture distributed only as TorchScript checkpoints). Public ungated checkpoint archive with no licence stated (all rights reserved by default). Benchmark test sets on Hugging Face under Apache-2.0 per the dataset card. Hosted MCP server with no stated terms of use. Training splits and fine-tuning code not yet released.
io: Cell-line transcriptome (log2 TPM) + compound SMILES, gene name and/or protein sequence (with dose and time for expression) -> drug sensitivity, drug-induced expression change, drug-protein binding, TF-gene association, gene dependency, mutation status and copy-number predictions
use_cases: Drug sensitivity and drug-induced expression prediction, drug-target binding, gene dependency prediction, multi-objective virtual compound screening
audit_note: Surfaced through the bio.rodeo feed. Verified on 2026-10-10 against the bioRxiv record and full text, the repository and its licence, a HEAD request and a zip file listing (tail range request only) of the checkpoint archive, and the Hugging Face dataset card. The released checkpoints are seven stage-2 task-specialized TorchScript modules plus a cell-line autoencoder; the stage-1 shared model, training splits and fine-tuning code are promised after acceptance. The weight archive carries no licence, so Apache-2.0 is confirmed for the inference code only. Pretraining data are cell-line measurements; single-cell, spatial and patient uses are author-reported adaptations. No weights were downloaded or run.

name: DistillPath
description: Compact 22M-parameter ViT-S/16 pathology tile encoders from ETH Zurich, distilled from frozen released pathology foundation models (H0-mini, Virchow2, UNI2-h, H-optimus-0) using only their final class and patch tokens on 6,000 public TCGA slides; students are initialised from kaiko ViT-S/16 (KS16) or ImageNet-21k ViT-S/16 (IS16). The best variant comes within 0.015 of Virchow2 on the seven-task EVA mean at about 29 times fewer parameters.
status: MIT code; six public ungated timm checkpoints on Hugging Face: kaiko-initialised KS16 weights under the Kaiko Non-Commercial Public License, ImageNet-initialised IS16 weights under CC-BY-NC-4.0 (UNI2-h and Virchow2 teachers) or Apache-2.0 (H-optimus-0 teacher). UNI2-h and Virchow2 terms bar commercial use of models trained on their outputs without approval. H0-mini-distilled variants are not released. Training slides are public TCGA.
io: H&E image tiles (224 x 224) -> 384-dimensional class-token and patch-token embeddings
use_cases: Lower-cost tile feature extraction for whole-slide image pipelines; tile-level tissue classification and nuclear segmentation; gene-expression prediction from H&E; scanner- and stain-robust tile retrieval
audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-10-10 from the arXiv abstract and HTML full text, the GitHub repository and licence API, hub API metadata and file listings for all six released checkpoints, their model cards and LICENSE files, and the UNI2-h, Virchow2 and H-optimus-0 hub gating text. Weights carry per-checkpoint licences (kaiko NC, CC-BY-NC-4.0, one Apache-2.0); the cards restate teacher licences and state the students contain no teacher weights, while UNI2-h and Virchow2 terms treat models trained on their outputs as derivatives barred from commercial use. Whether those teacher terms permit public release of such students was not settled. The paper's H0-mini-distilled variants were not found on the hub. No weights were downloaded or run.

name: CytoFormer
description: Cell-level H&E encoder fine-tuned end-to-end from UNI2-h on cell-type labels derived from paired Xenium spatial transcriptomics (15.4 million cells, 81 sections, 16 organs, 23 cell types). A per-organ head types each nucleus; the encoder's 1536-d embedding is released for reuse as a cell-level feature extractor.
status: Inference code and model definition under the Penn Academic Software License (internal research or non-commercial use; no redistribution without Penn's written permission; GitHub reports NOASSERTION); no training code. Weights labelled CC BY-NC 4.0 behind an automatic Hugging Face contact-sharing gate. The checkpoint is a fine-tune of UNI2-h, whose CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms bar redistribution and commercial use of derivatives; no upstream permission is stated.
io: H&E nucleus-centred 56 µm patch (224×224 px) + organ identifier -> organ-restricted cell-type label (23 types) and 1536-d cell embedding
use_cases: Cell typing on routine H&E slides across 16 organs, whole-section cell maps, linear-probe transfer and label-efficient interactive annotation for cell-level classification (author-reported)
audit_note: Verified on 2026-10-10 from the arXiv v1 full text, the GitHub README, licence file and file tree, the Hugging Face API and public card page, and the UNI2-h card. Training is supervised cell-type fine-tuning of UNI2-h (catalog record bfm-uni-uni2-h); transfer is author-reported and covers only cell-classification benchmarks. The gate was not passed, so the checkpoint (about 2.7 GB) was seen only in the file listing. The CC BY-NC 4.0 weight label conflicts with UNI2-h's no-redistribution, no-derivatives terms; the paper, README and visible card state no upstream permission.

name: DreaMS
aliases: Deep Representations Empowering the Annotation of Mass Spectra
description: 116M-parameter transformer pretrained by self-supervision (masked spectral peaks and chromatographic retention order) on millions of unannotated tandem mass spectra from the GeMS dataset mined from MassIVE GNPS; its spectrum representations are used directly or fine-tuned for small-molecule MS/MS annotation in metabolomics.
status: Open code + weights + data: code MIT; ungated checkpoints on the authors' Hugging Face repo (card MIT; the route the code downloads from) and on Zenodo (CC BY 4.0); GeMS pretraining data on Hugging Face (MIT label); free web app on a Hugging Face Space with no stated licence.
io: MS/MS spectra (e.g. .mgf) -> 1,024-dimensional spectrum embeddings; fine-tuned heads predict spectral similarity, molecular fingerprints, chemical properties and fluorine presence
use_cases: Spectrum annotation in untargeted metabolomics, spectral library and structural-analog search, molecular networking (DreaMS Atlas), molecular fingerprint and chemical property prediction, fluorine detection
audit_note: Verified 2026-10-10 from Crossref and Europe PMC (Nat Biotechnol online 2025-05-23, CC BY; ChemRxiv v1 posted 2023-12-01 under an earlier title), the repository (MIT LICENSE; README links paper, weights, data and web app), Zenodo 10997887 (CC BY 4.0; embedding_model.ckpt, ssl_model.ckpt) and the Hugging Face API (ungated, card MIT; the same two checkpoints at identical byte sizes plus a MassSpecGym embedding checkpoint and a TorchScript export). The code downloads weights from the Hugging Face repo. The two weight hosts carry different licence labels. The Zenodo weights record has no Zenodo DOI and lists the ChemRxiv DOI as its PID. Upstream MassIVE terms for GeMS were not reviewed. No weights were downloaded or run.

name: CTransPath
description: Self-supervised histopathology tile encoder that couples a convolutional stem with a Swin Transformer (Swin-T) backbone. It was pretrained with semantically-relevant contrastive learning (SRCL) on about 15 million unlabelled TCGA and PAIP patches, and the authors recommend it as a frozen histopathology feature extractor.
status: Open code and public ungated weights (author Google Drive link). LICENSE.md is GPL-3.0, but the README states availability for non-commercial academic purposes only, and these terms conflict. There is no separate weight licence. Non-commercial terms apply to at least one artifact or access route.
io: H&E histology tile (224 px; README suggests about 1.0 mpp first) -> tile-level embedding
use_cases: Frozen tile features for patch classification and retrieval, and weakly supervised whole-slide classification (multiple-instance learning). Fine-tuning for mitosis detection and gland segmentation.
audit_note: Older catalog gap, verified on 2026-10-10 from Crossref, Europe PMC (abstract, PMID 35952419), the GitHub licence API, the README and the Drive file page; no weights were downloaded. LICENSE.md is unmodified GPL-3.0, but the README License section restricts use to non-commercial academic purposes, so noncommercial is set to true and the GPL/NC conflict is left unresolved. The weights are on a personal Drive with no weight licence and no checksum, and they need a modified timm 0.5.4 build, also on Drive. The same repo hosts separate TransPath (MICCAI 2021) and MoCo v3 checkpoints; these are not part of this record, and TransPath is not an alias. Hugging Face copies are third-party re-uploads.

name: GRASP
description: Molecular graph Transformer (93.5M parameters) pretrained by replaced-token detection on 1.54B ZINC20 molecule presentations and then adapted with sparse labels from 642 ChEMBL assays; the released 50,000-step Step 2 encoder provides 768-d molecular embeddings for downstream property models.
status: Public ungated weights (Hugging Face) and code (GitHub, no tagged release) under CC BY-NC 4.0 per LICENSE file, NOTICE and model card; MolE-derived code inherits CC BY-NC 4.0; bundled DeBERTa code MIT. README licence line changed to MIT on 2026-10-05 without changing LICENSE or NOTICE (conflict; non-commercial reading applied). Training data not redistributed; no hosted API.
io: SMILES (2D molecular graph) -> 768-d molecular embedding (final-layer CLS); embedding + labelled data -> fine-tuned property predictor (full, LoRA or frozen encoder)
use_cases: ADMET property prediction by fine-tuning (full, LoRA or frozen encoder), molecular embeddings for downstream property models, molecular representation learning
audit_note: Preprint only (bioRxiv, v2 posted 2026-10-06); README and model card cite an arXiv identifier as pending. LICENSE, NOTICE, vendored MolE licence and model card apply CC BY-NC 4.0; the README has said MIT since a 2026-10-05 commit, unresolved, so the non-commercial reading is used. Reuses MolE code but pretrains its own encoder; not a MolE re-release. Downstream evaluation covers ADMET endpoints only. Weights listed, not downloaded or executed.

name: LDDM (Large Drug Discovery Model)
description: Pocket-conditioned 3D generative model covering constrained and unconstrained docking, fragment linking and growing, and de novo ligand design in one model, with a programmable sampler for synthesizable designs.
io: Protein pocket structure (+ optional ligand fragments or constraints) -> 3D ligand poses or generated ligands
status: Open MIT code; Zenodo weights: paper checkpoint CC BY-NC 4.0 (BindingNet data), BindingNet-free checkpoint MIT; no hosted API; Enamine REAL design needs a separate Enamine licence
use_cases: Structure-based drug design, docking, fragment linking and growing, synthesizable analogue design
audit_note: Adversarial review 2026-10-10. Preprint only (bioRxiv published=NA); re-check for a journal version. Terms are checkpoint-specific: lddm.ckpt is CC BY-NC 4.0 because of BindingNet training data, lddm_CDBB.ckpt and the other Zenodo files are MIT, and the Zenodo record-level licence field reads MIT, so the per-checkpoint wording must be preserved. The preprint links only the GitHub repository; the Zenodo weights record is endorsed through the official README, not the paper. Enamine REAL synthesizable design requires a licence from Enamine; the shipped 44,944-block space is SynSpace/Mcule-derived. Weights verified from Zenodo metadata and file listing only, never downloaded or executed.

name: Zatom-1
description: Transformer (80M-300M parameters) trained with a multimodal flow-matching objective over discrete atom types and continuous 3D geometries, jointly pretrained on QM9 small molecules and MP20 crystals, with further GEOM-Drugs, QMOF and OMol25 pretraining checkpoints; the generative pretraining initialises downstream property, energy and force prediction.
status: LBNL modified-BSD code licence; public ungated weights on Hugging Face (card: MIT) and Zenodo (record: CC BY 4.0); no hosted API
io: Sampling from noise -> 3D molecules or crystals (atom types, coordinates, lattice); 3D molecular or crystal structure -> property, energy and force predictions via finetuned heads
use_cases: 3D small-molecule and crystal generation, molecular and materials property prediction, energy/force prediction, transfer learning
audit_note: Workshop paper (ICLR 2026 FM4Science) on arXiv. Licence labels differ across distributions but all are permissive: LBNL modified-BSD for code (the paper says 'permissive BSD'), an MIT tag in the HF card YAML (no LICENSE file in the HF repo), and CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo record. The README downloads checkpoints from Zenodo; HF is an author-org mirror (org members are paper authors). Chemistry/materials model whose link to biology runs through small and drug-like molecules and an OMol25 checkpoint. Successor Zatom-2 (October 2026) is held for missing artifacts. Weights not executed.

name: AIMNet2
description: Atoms-in-molecules neural network potential for neutral and charged organic and element-organic molecules (up to 14 elements) combining learned short-range and physics-based long-range terms; family members cover reactive pathways (AIMNet2-rxn), open-shell species and palladium chemistry.
status: Open code + ungated weights (MIT) on GitHub and Hugging Face; AIMNet2 training data (MIT) on CMU KiltHub; AIMNet2-rxn archived on Zenodo (MIT); public web demo
io: 3D molecular structure with total charge (and spin multiplicity for the open-shell model) -> energies, forces, atomic charges, Hessians; stress for periodic systems
use_cases: Molecular dynamics, conformer search and torsion scans, reaction-path and transition-state search, drug-like and element-organic chemistry
audit_note: Family record; members differ in element and charge coverage (AIMNet2-rxn: closed-shell, net-neutral C, H, N, O). All five Isayev-lab HF repos (wb97m-d3, 2025, nse, pd, rxn) are ungated MIT; the AIMNet2 training datasets on CMU KiltHub are MIT; the AIMNet2-rxn reaction training set was not found among released files. The Science Advances article is CC BY-NC 4.0 and the Chem Sci article CC BY 3.0. These are article licences only, not code, weight or data terms. Publisher pages blocked automated fetch (403); metadata and full texts were read via Crossref and Europe PMC. Year follows the 2023 ChemRxiv preprint listed by Crossref. Not executed.

name: DPA4 / DPA4C (DeePMD-kit)
description: Universal equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials implemented in DeePMD-kit: DPA4 (SeZM architecture) targets accuracy, and DPA4C is a compact, compressible variant for high-throughput, large-scale MD. Checkpoints trained on OMol25 (biomolecules, metal complexes, electrolytes) are intended for molecular systems; DPA4C-OMol has much higher molecular errors than DPA4-OMol. Materials checkpoints (OMat24) are released separately.
status: Open code (LGPL-3.0, DeePMD-kit 3.2.0+); public ungated checkpoints on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC 4.0 (declared in model-card metadata); training data are third-party public datasets
io: Atomic structure with total charge and spin multiplicity -> energies and forces
use_cases: Energy/force prediction and MD for molecules within OMol25 chemical space and for materials; large-scale MD (DPA4C); fine-tuning to system-specific potentials
audit_note: Materials-first family (DPA4 headline benchmark: Matbench Discovery); only the OMol25-trained checkpoints target molecules. On the OMol25 OOD composition split, DPA4C energy MAEs are 16.77-40.97 kcal/mol versus 0.92-8.02 for DPA4. Released OMol checkpoints are Air/Mini/Nano/Neo/Plus; DPA4-Pro is not released. MatPES-trained variants are benchmarked but not on the hub. Neither paper's availability statement mentions weights; the HF org is referenced by DeePMD-kit's pretrained registry, though the OMol repos are not listed there. Weight licence is CC BY-NC 4.0 in card metadata only, with no licence file; code is LGPL-3.0. Older DPA-2/DPA-3 checkpoints (CC BY 4.0) not assessed. Preprints only; weights not executed.

name: KERMT (Contrastive KERMT)
description: Graph-transformer molecular encoder for small-molecule property prediction. KERMT (Merck and NVIDIA, 2025) is an accelerated GROVER reimplementation for multitask fine-tuning that used the published GROVER weights.
